Travel Planning Guide — Researched September 2026

Rio de Janeiro
for Carnival 2027

Rio de Janeiro sightseeing, Camarote Mar, and Iguazu Falls — February 6–15, 2027. New York → Buenos Aires → Rio → Camarote Mar → Iguazu (Brazilian side + Argentine side) → São Paulo → New York. The São Paulo pre-Carnival week (Jan 29–Feb 5) has its own tab below.

Feb 6–15, 2027 9 nights Peak Carnival week 2BR · 2BA required South Zone focus
São Paulo · January 29 – February 5, 2027
Pre-Carnival week · São Paulo → coast → Rio
Who
Land in São Paulo on Friday, Jan 29, 2027. Spend the pre-Carnival week driving the São Paulo–Rio coast and reach Rio de Janeiro by Friday, Feb 5 (night) — in time for the Rio + Iguazu · Feb 6 – Feb 15 tab.
Plan
Day-by-day itinerary below: São Paulo city (Jan 30), an Embu das Artes day trip (Jan 31), then the coastal road trip — Ubatuba (2 nights) → Paraty (2 nights) → Rio. Backup itineraries (Angra dos Reis / Ilha Grande, Ilhabela, other parts of Brazil) follow the main plan. Assumes a one-way rental car: pick up in São Paulo Jan 31, return in Rio Feb 5 (the taxa de retorno one-way fee is quoted at booking) — see “Rental Car vs. Public Transportation” below for why.
Feb 6 →
Continue in Rio de Janeiro — switch to the Rio + Iguazu · Feb 6 – Feb 15 tab.

Day-by-Day Itinerary

São Paulo → Embu das Artes → Ubatuba → Paraty → Rio de Janeiro. Eight days: one São Paulo city day, one folk-art day trip, four beach days, arriving Rio on Feb 5 night. Distances and drive times are approximate — check live traffic on the day.

Fri, Jan 29 — Land São Paulo
Arrive · settle in · easy evening
Arrive
Land at GRU (São Paulo/Guarulhos). Transfer to hotel — Jardins, Pinheiros, or Vila Mariana are the best bases (safe, walkable, good restaurants).
Evening
Easy first night: stroll Paulista Avenue, early dinner nearby, recover from the flight. No ambitious plans on arrival day.
Sat, Jan 30 — São Paulo: only-in-Brazil day
Padaria · Centro histórico · Mercadão · Liberdade · MASP · samba night
7:30 AM
Padaria breakfast: pão na chapa + pingado. The corner bakery is Brazil's morning parliament — bread griddled in butter until the edges crisp, dunked in coffee with milk, a ritual hundreds of millions of Brazilians perform daily. No café in New York does this. In and out in 30 minutes; pão francês has no egg, butter is dairy — strict-vegetarian safe.
8:30 AM
Pátio do Colégio. The 1554 Jesuit mission where São Paulo was founded — the birth certificate of a 22-million-person megacity, on the exact spot. Compact: 30–40 minutes is enough. Uber to Centro; daytime only, minimal valuables, crossbody bag.
9:05 AM
Sé Cathedral (30 min). One of the largest neo-Gothic churches on Earth — 111m towers — with the marco zero plaque out front, the exact point from which every São Paulo distance is measured, and Brazilian plants and animals carved into the stonework where European saints would normally be. Crypt if open.
9:40 AM
Edifício Copan — photo stop. Niemeyer's 1954 serpent: a 32-story residential block bent into a 100-meter concrete wave housing over a thousand apartments. Social housing as sculpture — the idea that an ordinary apartment block should be art is pure Brazilian modernism.
10:00 AM–12:00 PM
Mercado Municipal (Mercadão). A 1933 market hall wrapped in 12,000 m² of stained glass — then the real event: tasting through the stalls. Cupuaçu, graviola, jabuticaba eaten off the stem — fruits that simply don't exist in North American markets. Mid-morning: pastel de queijo (cheese — specify, and ask about shared frying oil). Market retail runs 6 AM–6 PM.
12:00 PM
Lunch: comida a quilo. The pay-by-weight buffet born in São Paulo and now a national institution — 30+ hot dishes, pile a plate, pay per kilo. The most democratic restaurant format on Earth and total control for a strict vegetarian: rice, grilled vegetables, salad, fresh exotic juice. Ask “o feijão tem carne?” — some beans are cooked with meat.
1:30–3:30 PM
Liberdade. Uber ~15 min. The largest Japanese diaspora on Earth has its capital here: streets strung with red torii lamps, a century of Japanese-Brazilian fusion you can taste on foot. This neighborhood cannot exist anywhere else. Strict-veg note: stick to fruit, açaí, and tapioca from street stalls — most baked Japanese sweets contain egg, so ask before buying.
4:00–6:30 PM
Avenida Paulista + MASP. Lina Bo Bardi's 1968 museum is a concrete-and-glass box floating 8 meters in the air on four pillars, with masterpieces hung on freestanding glass easels instead of walls — the Southern Hemisphere's greatest collection, displayed in a way no US or Canadian museum dares. Open daily except Mondays (verify); book online (free Thursday evenings reported — verify). Then walk the avenue itself, the financial and cultural heart of the city.
7:00 PM
Hotel rest. Feet up — you've earned it.
8:00 PM
Dinner in Bixiga. São Paulo's Italian quarter, where late-19th-century immigrants built cantinas still serving the same red-sauce feasts — and where the Vai-Vai samba school was born, so Italian and Afro-Brazilian culture share one street. Dinner here is eating the city's immigration history. Order vegetarian pasta or pizza; confirm fresh pasta has no egg (dried pasta is safe).
9:30–11:30 PM
Live samba: Ó do Borogodó (Pinheiros). A tiny bar where samba de mesa happens inches from your table — musicians crowded around, no stage, no distance. In Brazil samba isn't a show, it's a conversation, and this is the room where you finally hear it properly. Check the week's schedule before going; Uber home.
Getting around
Uber all day — no rental car in the city. São Paulo traffic is among the worst in the Americas, weekday rodízio rules ban cars from the expanded center by license plate (a rental could be illegal to drive on your day), and parking is scarce. Uber door-to-door is also the security play. Pick up the car Jan 31 morning — one-way rental: São Paulo pickup, Rio return Feb 5. The coast is where it transforms the trip.
Sun, Jan 31 — Embu das Artes day trip
Folk-art fair · colonial center · rental car pickup
7:00 AM
Wake up + padaria breakfast. Pão na chapa + pingado near the hotel. Eat light — you're driving at 9. Lay out the day bag: sun hat, water, cash and card for the fair, and a bargaining mindset.
8:00 AM
Pick up the rental car. São Paulo city agency. Paperwork: US driver's license (valid for tourists up to 180 days), passport, credit card in the driver's name; an International Driving Permit is recommended backup. Ask for the Sem Parar toll tag — optional, but it saves fumbling for cash at every booth. One-way rental: Localiza, Movida and Unidas all allow São Paulo pickup → Rio return Feb 5; the taxa de retorno one-way fee (roughly R$500 on this route) is quoted at booking.
9:00 AM
Drive to Embu das Artes. ~40 min via Rodovia Raposo Tavares. Easy highway — your shakedown drive before Monday's coastal road. Get the seat, mirrors and Waze sorted now, not on the serra.
10:00 AM
Feira de Arte e Artesanato opens. Arrive at opening for the best pieces. The fair fills the colonial streets — wood carvings, ceramics, lace, carnival masks, paintings from every Brazilian region. This is Brazil's craft capital, born when 1960s artists turned a colonial town into the country's great folk-art fair. Runs Sat–Sun ~10 AM–6 PM.
11:00 AM
Work the fair + side streets. The side lanes hold smaller ateliers and better prices — bargaining is normal, start ~20% below asking. Look for what you can't find elsewhere: Nordestino woodcuts, Bahian ceramics, carnival masks.
12:00 PM
Colonial center: Igreja Nossa Senhora do Rosário. The 18th-century Jesuit church and its sacred-art museum — the reason Embu exists at all, a Jesuit settlement turned art town. 30–40 minutes, cool and quiet inside.
1:00 PM
Lunch in Embu. Comida a quilo or a historic-center restaurant — rice, vegetables, salad, fresh juice. Ask “o feijão tem carne?” about the beans. Unhurried — the fair runs till 6, no rush.
2:00 PM
Galleries + antique shops. The streets around the Largo hold proper galleries and antique dealers — the serious buying happens here rather than at the stalls. Even just browsing is a crash course in Brazilian popular art.
3:00 PM
Drive back to São Paulo. ~40 min. Aim to be back before the late-afternoon traffic builds.
4:00 PM
Fuel up + hotel rest. Fill the tank tonight so Monday starts clean. Feet up for an hour — tomorrow is the coastal drive.
5:00 PM
Pack for the coast. Lay out the beach kit: swimwear, towel, sunscreen, hat, water shoes. Confirm tomorrow's route on the phone — Tamoios (SP-099) → BR-101 Rio-Santos west to Ubatuba — and download offline maps.
6:00 PM
Buffer hour. Nothing scheduled, deliberately — nap, read, or a slow coffee. The last two days were dense; tonight is about arriving at the coast rested.
7:00 PM
Dinner near the hotel. Keep it light and early — Pinheiros or Vila Mariana have plenty of vegetarian-friendly kitchens. Confirm fresh pasta has no egg if you order pasta.
8:00 PM
Early night. Bags by the door; license, passport and rental papers in the daypack. You're on the road at 8:30 AM — tomorrow the road trip begins.
Mon, Feb 1 — Drive to Ubatuba
Tamoios descent · first beach afternoon · Itaguá evening
7:00 AM
Wake up, padaria breakfast, checkout. Eat well — the next proper meal is lunch in Ubatuba. Load the car: bags in the trunk, daypack with documents, water and snacks up front. Nothing visible on the seats.
8:00 AM
Final checks + depart São Paulo. Tires, fuel (full tank from last night), Waze set for Ubatuba via SP-099. Monday morning — leave by 8 to beat São Paulo's rush hour; the Tamoios route heads northeast, away from the worst of it. The daylight-only rule starts now — every coastal leg is planned to finish before dark.
9:00 AM
On the Tamoios. Climbing out of the São Paulo plateau, then the descent begins: Atlantic rainforest (Mata Atlântica) closing in on both sides, the air getting warmer and wetter with every curve. Tolls: Sem Parar tag or manual booths. Keep right, let faster traffic pass.
10:00 AM
Reach the coast, turn onto the Rio-Santos. Caraguatatuba → west on BR-101. The road now hugs the Atlantic — islands offshore, rainforest on the inland side. This is the famous stretch: the drive is the attraction, not just transit. Use the signed mirantes (viewpoints); never stop on blind curves.
11:00 AM
Arrive Ubatuba, settle in. Check in or drop bags. Ubatuba is São Paulo state's surf capital — 100+ beaches along rainforest-backed coastline, more variety than anywhere else on this route. Itaguá is the town hub; the best beaches are 10–30 km out, which is exactly why you have the car.
12:00 PM
Lunch. Beach kiosk (barraca) or comida a quilo in town. Strict-veg beach kit: queijo coalho (grilled cheese on a stick — dairy, no egg, safe), milho verde (corn on the cob), açaí, fresh coconut water. Hydrate — the coast is humid.
1:00 PM
Praia do Félix. Drive out to the cove (~15–20 min from town). Remote, crystalline water, rainforest walls on both sides — the postcard version of the Brazilian coast. Settle in: swim, shade, nothing scheduled.
2:00 PM
Beach afternoon continues. Snorkel if you brought gear, walk the cove end to end, or do nothing at all — this hour is the trip exhaling. Reapply sunscreen; the equatorial sun burns fast even through cloud.
3:00 PM
More beach, or hop to Toninhas. Stay at Félix, or drive to Praia das Toninhas for easier swimming and more kiosks. Beach-hopping is trivial with the car — that was the whole point of renting it.
4:00 PM
Last swim, head back toward town. Rinse off and change at the hotel. The sun drops fast near the equator — plan to be off the sand by 5.
5:00 PM
Sunset at the Itaguá waterfront. Golden hour over the bay, fishing boats coming in, the town switching on. Açaí or coconut water on the promenade.
6:00 PM
Rest at the hotel. Shower, decompress. Decide tonight's question: tomorrow — Ilha Anchieta boat trip, or the wild beaches (Cedro, Vermelha do Norte)? Decide now so the morning starts clean.
7:00 PM
Dinner in Itaguá. The walkable evening strip: local restaurants, cachaça bars, the town's night pulse. Vegetarian-friendly kitchens are easy here — moqueca de palmito if you spot it (ask “a farofa tem bacon?” about the farofa).
8:00 PM
Easy night. Early rest — tomorrow is the full Ubatuba beach day, and the wild beaches need a morning start.
Driving rules
1. Daylight only, always — never this road at night (poor lighting, winding serra stretches). 2. Stick to the main highways; ignore GPS “shortcuts,” especially near Rio (stay on BR-101 → Av. Brasil). 3. Doors locked, windows up, valuables out of sight. 4. Eat and refuel at proper postos (highway service stations). 5. Jan/Feb is the rainy season — if a serra downpour kills visibility, wait it out at a posto.
Tue, Feb 2 — Ubatuba: Ilha Anchieta boat day
Prison-island ruins · snorkeling · Itaguá evening
7:00 AM
Wake up, padaria breakfast. Pack: swimwear, towel, sunscreen, hat, water, snacks, snorkel gear — and mosquito repellent, essential on the island's trails. Confirm yesterday's boat booking.
8:00 AM
Drive to the pier (Itaguá / Enseada). Schooners (escunas) depart in the morning; ~30-min crossing. Ask the operator's itinerary — maximize time on Anchieta itself. Park entry ~R$15/person, payable at the island.
9:00 AM
Crossing to Ilha Anchieta. Open water, the coastline falling behind — the island rises out of the Atlantic ahead. A state park reachable only by boat.
10:00 AM
Praia do Presídio: prison ruins + museum. A former penal colony — political prisoners, a 1952 rebellion — turned nature reserve. The museum and staff tell the stories; allow 45–60 minutes.
11:00 AM
Forest trails to the beaches. Praia das Palmas (white sand, calm clear water — the island's best swimming) or Praia do Engenho (natural rock pools, the “aquário natural”). Short trails through Atlantic forest; many beaches are deserted and reachable only on foot.
12:00 PM
Swim + snorkel. Palmas for floating in glassy water; Engenho's pools for colorful fish in the shallows.
1:00 PM
Lunch: picnic. The island has limited food infrastructure — pack fruit, cheese, tapioca and water. Eat in the shade; midday sun is fierce.
2:00 PM
More pools and trails. The Saco Grande trail (viewpoint over the surrounding islands) if energy allows — 30–60 min round trip.
3:00 PM
Last swim, rinse, back to the pier. Day boats leave ~4 PM — don't miss the return.
4:00 PM
Boat back to Ubatuba.
5:00 PM
Hotel: shower, rest.
6:00 PM
Sunset on the Itaguá waterfront.
7:00 PM
Dinner in Itaguá. The walkable evening strip: local restaurants, cachaça bars, the town's night pulse.
8:00 PM
Pack for Paraty; early night. Tomorrow's drive is short (~1h15m) but the historic center deserves a full afternoon.
Instead
Wild beaches day: Praia do Cedro (trail-access cove) + Praia Vermelha do Norte (red-tinged sand, striking). Full-day, low-structure; the car makes the 10–30 km beach hops easy.
Wed, Feb 3 — Drive to Paraty + Trindade
UNESCO colonial center · Cachadaço natural pools
7:30 AM
Breakfast, checkout, load the car. Short drive today — no rush, but an early arrival buys you the historic center in good light.
9:00 AM
Depart Ubatuba → Paraty (~1h15m via BR-101 Rio-Santos). Rainforest on one side, island-dotted sea on the other — one of Brazil's most scenic coastal drives.
10:30 AM
Arrive Paraty, check in / drop bags. Leave the car — the historic center is entirely walkable and car-free.
11:00 AM
First wander: the UNESCO historic center. Paraty + Ilha Grande form Brazil's first mixed World Heritage site. “Pé-de-moleque” cobblestones — the streets flood at high tide by design, washing themselves clean — whitewashed houses with colorful trim, 18th-century churches: Santa Rita and the Matriz (Nossa Senhora dos Remédios).
12:00 PM
Casa da Cultura + cachaça shops. Galleries and alambique shops — Paraty's name was once synonymous with cachaça across Brazil, and the distilleries around town are the real thing.
1:00 PM
Lunch in the historic center. Comida a quilo or a colonial restaurant — this is moqueca de palmito country (ask “a farofa tem bacon?” about the farofa).
2:00 PM
Siesta at the hotel. The center is best in late-afternoon light anyway — recharge for Trindade.
3:00 PM
Drive to Trindade (~40 min). Park in the fishing village.
4:00 PM
Praia do Meio → trail to the Cachadaço natural pools. 40–50 min medium trail through Atlantic forest (or a small boat from Praia do Meio, ~US$4 cash). Volcanic rocks block the open sea, leaving calm, transparent, shallow water — a natural aquarium. No kiosks: bring water, collect all trash.
5:00 PM
The pools + optional Pedra que Engole. Swim with the small fish; the adventurous can try the “swallowing stone” natural waterslide nearby (20-min trail, only on sunny days — a local guide is advised for the rock slide). Start back before dark.
6:00 PM
Walk/boat back, drive to Paraty (~40 min).
7:30 PM
Dinner in the historic center. Paraty at night — lit churches, live music drifting from the bars — is the most atmospheric the town gets.
8:30 PM
Night stroll; confirm tomorrow's Mamanguá boat at the pier or through the hotel.
Thu, Feb 4 — Paraty boat day: Saco do Mamanguá
Brazil's only fjord · islands · historic center evening
7:00 AM
Breakfast. Pack: swimwear, towel, sunscreen, hat, water, snacks, cash. Confirm the boat.
8:00 AM
Board at the Paraty pier. Schooner day trip — booked the evening before.
9:00 AM
Depart into the bay. Island-dotted water, the colonial town shrinking behind you.
10:00 AM
First swim stop. Island beaches, snorkeling over clear water.
11:00 AM
Saco do Mamanguá. Brazil's only tropical fjord — a deep green inlet walled by rainforest peaks, still and silent. The boat noses in slowly; this is the day's centerpiece.
12:00 PM
Cruise + lunch. Served on board or at a beach-restaurant stop (confirm when booking). Vegetarians are easy — rice, beans, salad and grilled vegetables are standard even where fish is the headline.
1:00 PM
More swim stops: Lagoa Azul, Ilha Comprida — the classic Paraty bay circuit.
2:00 PM
Last swim, slow cruise back.
3:00 PM
Back at the pier. Rest at the hotel.
4:00 PM
Pack for the Rio drive + rest. Bags ready tonight — tomorrow is the 4-hour leg.
5:00 PM
Historic center golden hour. Churches, waterfront, the light on the cobblestones.
6:00 PM
Cachaça tasting at an alambique shop. A proper aged cachaça or Gabriela — Paraty's signature.
7:30 PM
Dinner in the historic center.
8:30 PM
Live music / night stroll. Early-ish night — the Rio drive starts at 8:30 AM.
Fri, Feb 5 — Drive to Rio
Arrive Rio · return car · night in the city
7:00 AM
Breakfast, checkout, load the car. Full tank before leaving Paraty.
8:30 AM
Depart Paraty → Rio (~4 hrs via BR-101). The last coastal leg — daylight only, as always.
10:00 AM
On the road: Angra dos Reis bay. The Costa Verde's island maze offshore — 365 islands in the bay. Stay on BR-101; ignore any GPS “shortcut.”
11:00 AM
Costa Verde → Rio metro. The road straightens as the city approaches. Doors locked, valuables out of sight.
12:00 PM
Av. Brasil → Copacabana. Stay on the main highway into the Zona Sul — no side streets, no matter what the GPS suggests.
1:00 PM
Return the rental car at a Localiza/Movida agency near Copacabana — not the airport, since you're staying in the city (check the agency list when booking). Hand over the keys: Uber for the entire Rio leg from here. The one-way fee (taxa de retorno) was quoted at booking. Check in to the hotel.
2:00 PM
Lunch near the hotel, rest. The drive is done.
4:00 PM
Light orientation: Copacabana promenade. The famous wave-pattern sidewalk, your first look at the Rio beachfront — the real beach days start Feb 6+.
5:00 PM
Sunset from the promenade.
7:00 PM
Easy dinner near the hotel. Early rest.
8:00 PM
Early night. Tomorrow the Rio leg begins — see the Rio + Iguazu · Feb 6 – Feb 15 tab.

Backup Itineraries

Alternatives to the main plan above — same Jan 29 – Feb 5 window, different coast stops or different parts of Brazil entirely.

Backup A — Angra dos Reis + Ilha Grande
Swap Ubatuba for the island bay · Feb 1–2
Change
Replace the two Ubatuba nights (Feb 1–2) with Angra dos Reis: São Paulo → Angra ~4 hrs. The bay holds 365 islands — take a full boat day among the islands (Ilha Grande, Lagoa Azul) instead of conventional beach days.
Keep
Everything else unchanged: Jan 29–31 São Paulo, Feb 3–4 Paraty, Feb 5 → Rio (~2.5 hrs from Angra).
Note
Ilha Grande has no roads and no rolling luggage — stay in Angra and visit by boat unless you're packed in backpacks. See “Ferry and Boat Requirements” below.
Backup B — Add Ilhabela
Most beach-heavy version · island + waterfalls
Change
Drop the Embu das Artes day trip (Jan 31) and add Ilhabela: drive to São Sebastião, 15-min ferry to the island. Waterfalls (Cachoeira da Toca), Bonete and Castelhanos beaches, no Uber on the island — rental car or island taxis.
Shape
Jan 29–30 São Paulo → Jan 31–Feb 1 Ilhabela → Feb 2 Ubatuba → Feb 3–4 Paraty → Feb 5 Rio. Five beach/island days, one full city day.
Backup C — Other parts of Brazil
Fly out for the pre-Carnival week instead of driving the coast
Salvador, Bahia
Fly São Paulo → Salvador for Feb 1–4: Pelourinho (UNESCO colonial center), Afro-Brazilian culture and music, Atlantic beaches (Porto da Barra, Flamengo). Brazil's most culturally distinct city — a completely different week from the coast drive. Return to São Paulo or fly direct toward Rio by Feb 5.
Florianópolis
Fly São Paulo → Florianópolis (“Magic Island”): 42 beaches, dunes, lagoons, a younger surf-town energy. Closer and cheaper to reach than Salvador; pair with 1–2 São Paulo days on either side.
Keep
Jan 29–31 São Paulo stays as the anchor; only the Feb 1–4 coast block is replaced. Back in Rio by Feb 5 night either way.

Beach Destination

Flying into São Paulo, driving toward Rio — the SP–Rio coastal corridor passes through some of Brazil's finest beaches. The route (SP-099 Tamoios highway to the coast, then BR-101 Rio-Santos highway) offers a genuine choice of where to stop. Below are the top 3 destinations worth considering for this specific road trip.

Quick Comparison

Destination São Paulo → → Rio Suggested Stay Main Advantage
Paraty ~4 hrs ~4 hrs 2 nights True midpoint · UNESCO colonial town + beaches
Ubatuba ~2.5 hrs ~5 hrs 2 nights Most beach variety · closest to SP · best natural setting
Angra dos Reis ~4 hrs ~2.5 hrs 2 nights 365 islands · calm bay · most dramatic scenery
Best-Fit Guide
Choose based on what matters to you
Easiest Integration
Paraty — true midpoint with roughly equal drives on both sides. No detour. Colonial town adds cultural depth that a pure beach stop lacks.
Classic Beach
Ubatuba — closest to São Paulo, maximum beach variety. Best if you want 2 full beach days and can manage the longer drive to Rio on departure.
Special Experience
Angra dos Reis — 365 islands in a sheltered tropical bay. Best if you want one day on a boat among islands rather than a conventional beach holiday.

Top Choices

Option 1 — Paraty
Best for easiest road-trip integration · Costa Verde · UNESCO World Heritage
Why Consider
  • UNESCO World Heritage colonial town — one of Brazil's most beautiful preserved historic centers, with pedestrian-only cobblestone streets
  • True geographic midpoint: ~4 hrs from São Paulo, ~2.5 hrs to Rio
  • Access to exceptional beaches including Praia de Trindade and Praia do Sono
  • Pousadas, restaurants, and daily boat trips to offshore islands available from the town
Drive
São Paulo → Paraty: ~4 hrs (approx. 290 km via SP-099 Tamoios highway + BR-101)
Paraty → Rio: ~2.5 hrs (approx. 250 km via BR-101)
Stay
2 nights recommended.
Beach Experience
The town sits on a calm bay. The finest beaches — Praia de Trindade (30 min drive, exceptional clear water and rainforest backdrop) and Praia do Sono (short hike from the road) — are among the best on the Costa Verde. Boat trips to offshore islands depart daily from the waterfront.
February
February is Paraty's rainiest month. Heavy downpours are common. The historic colonial center historically floods during major rain events. Despite this, the surrounding rainforest is at its most lush and the bay is beautiful. Plan outdoor activities for mornings; have covered pousada time in the afternoons.
Main Tradeoff
  • February is Paraty's wettest month — the highest rain risk of the three options
  • Best beaches require a car or boat trip from the colonial center (not walkable)
Option 2 — Ubatuba
Best for classic beach destination · Litoral Norte de São Paulo
Why Consider
  • ~100 beaches across 70 km of coastline — the greatest beach variety on the entire SP–Rio corridor
  • Atlantic rainforest descends directly to the sand on most beaches
  • Closest major beach destination to São Paulo — only 2.5 hrs, the shortest first leg of the three options
  • Less developed than Ilhabela or Búzios — more natural and less commercial
Drive
São Paulo → Ubatuba: ~2.5 hrs (approx. 230 km via SP-099 Tamoios highway)
Ubatuba → Rio: ~5 hrs (approx. 320 km via BR-101, Paraty, Angra dos Reis)
Stay
2 nights strongly recommended — one night barely allows for a single beach visit.
Beach Experience
Praia do Félix, Praia da Fortaleza, Praia Vermelha do Norte, and Praia Itamambuca are all highly rated. Each beach has a distinct character — from calm bay to open Atlantic surf. Water temperature is 25°C+ in February. The rainforest and granite rock framing is extraordinary.
February
Peak summer season. Warm, humid, with brief afternoon storms typical of the Atlantic coastal summer. Water is warm and inviting. Beaches are busy but spread across many options — you can find quieter spots. Most affordable of the three destinations.
Main Tradeoff
  • Ubatuba → Rio is a long 5-hour drive — the most demanding departure day of the three options
  • Best suited for those arriving in São Paulo 3+ days before Carnival starts
Option 3 — Angra dos Reis
Best for scenic / special experience · Bay of Islands
Why Consider
  • 365 islands in a sheltered tropical bay — one of the most visually dramatic coastlines in Brazil
  • Bay beaches are calm and clear, protected from Atlantic ocean swell
  • Same drive time as Paraty from SP (~4 hrs) and to Rio (~2.5 hrs) — practical midpoint
  • Gateway to Ilha Grande, one of Brazil's most acclaimed islands, accessible by ferry from Angra
Drive
São Paulo → Angra dos Reis: ~4 hrs (approx. 300 km via BR-116 Presidente Dutra + SP-055)
Angra dos Reis → Rio: ~2.5 hrs (approx. 160 km via BR-101)
Stay
2 nights recommended — one day should be spent on a boat trip among the islands.
Beach Experience
The real attraction is the bay itself. A day boat trip visits calm beaches on uninhabited islands — turquoise water, no infrastructure, genuine tropical bay experience. Town beaches are pleasant, but the 365 islands are what make Angra genuinely different from other destinations on this corridor.
February
Hot, humid, and rainy — peak season. The enclosed bay provides shelter from ocean swell, so swimming conditions remain good even during rain. Boat trip operators are plentiful. Book accommodation early; February is heavily booked throughout the region.
Main Tradeoff
  • Best experience requires a boat rental or organized boat trip — adds cost and advance planning
  • Town beaches without a boat trip are pleasant but not the primary reason to choose Angra over Paraty

Road Trip Routes

Via Paraty
Easiest integration · balanced on both sides
Route
São Paulo → SP-099 Tamoios → Caraguatatuba → coast road → Paraty (~4 hrs) → BR-101 → Angra dos Reis → Rio de Janeiro (~4 hrs further)
Total
~8 hrs driving total, split across 2 days with a 2-night Paraty stop.
Via Ubatuba
Short first day · long second day
Route
São Paulo → SP-099 Tamoios → Ubatuba (~2.5 hrs) → BR-101 Rio-Santos → Paraty → Angra dos Reis → Rio de Janeiro (~5 hrs further)
Total
~7.5 hrs driving total, split across 2 days — shorter drive Day 1, longer drive Day 3.
Via Angra dos Reis
Island focus · same balance as Paraty
Route
São Paulo → BR-116 Presidente Dutra → SP-055 Padre Manoel da Nóbrega → Angra dos Reis (~4 hrs) → BR-101 → Rio de Janeiro (~2.5 hrs further)
Total
~6.5 hrs driving total, split across 2 days with a 2-night Angra stop.

Recommendation for Planning

🗺

The key tradeoff is position on the route and what you want from the stop.

Paraty or Angra dos Reis are the most practical choices for a clean road trip: ~4 hrs from SP, ~2.5 hrs to Rio, balanced on both sides. Choose Paraty for the colonial town experience and easier beach access by car. Choose Angra dos Reis for the island-bay experience and boat trip.

Ubatuba is the right choice if you want the most beach variety and can accommodate a long 5-hour drive to Rio. Best for those arriving in São Paulo 3 or more days before Carnival begins.

February rain note: All three experience summer afternoon rain. Paraty's February rainfall is significantly higher than Ubatuba or Angra — if rain minimisation matters, Ubatuba or Angra have a clear edge.

Full Corridor Research

Comprehensive evaluation of every major coastal destination between São Paulo and Rio — including destinations not covered in the three-stop summary above. Research conducted September 2026.

Two corridors: Litoral Norte (SP state) runs Santos → Guarujá → Bertioga → Caraguatatuba → São Sebastião/Ilhabela → Ubatuba. Costa Verde (RJ state) continues Paraty → Angra dos Reis/Ilha Grande → Mangaratiba → Rio. Ubatuba sits at the boundary.
SP State · 55 km from SP

Santos

Port city · World's longest beachfront garden · Urban waterfront

Half-day

Recommended visit

SP → Santos

1h drive · 1h 30m bus (Cometa from Jabaquara)

Santos → Rio

5–6h via BR-101 coastal route

Ferry / Boat

No (optional for Guarujá)

Car needed?

No — fully walkable waterfront

Worth stopping?

Yes — best half-day stop on route

Overnight?

Not justified

Waterfront: The Orla e Jardins da Praia de Santos is Guinness-certified as the world's largest beachfront garden — 7 km of landscaped gardens, sculptures, bike paths, cafés, and restaurants along the shore. Entry is free. This is a genuine, impressive urban waterfront, not a generic promenade.

Other attractions: Museu Pelé (Pelé museum in the original stadium area), Monte Serrat hilltop tram with bay views, historic coffee exchange buildings (early 20th-century mercantile architecture), day trip to Guarujá by ferry.

Beach quality: Average by Brazilian standards — clean, long, but water is not crystal clear. The beach is not the reason to visit; the waterfront garden and city character are.

SP State · 80 km from SP

Guarujá

Beach resort · São Paulo weekend destination

Half-day

If combined with Santos

SP → Guarujá

1h 30m drive

Ferry from Santos

10–15 min, frequent, cheap

Car needed?

No for main beach strip

Worth stopping?

Only combined with Santos

Best beaches: Pitangueiras (resort strip), Enseada (calm), Tombo (surf). Water quality better than Santos. The waterfront is resort-style with hotels and restaurants. As a standalone destination on the SP–Rio route it does not distinguish itself enough to justify a dedicated stop — better beaches exist further along the route. Works as a Santos extension for a beach afternoon after the Orla garden walk.

SP State · 100 km from SP

Bertioga

Quiet beach town · Colonial fort · Nature

2–3h max

Pass-through only

Best attraction: Forte São João (1532) — one of Brazil's oldest colonial fortifications. Pleasant beaches, calm and uncrowded compared to Guarujá. Waterfalls at Riviera de São Lourenço. Limited tourist infrastructure and no compelling waterfront. Adequate as a 2-hour detour; not worth a dedicated stop on the main SP–Rio itinerary.

SP State · 200 km from SP

São Sebastião

Ilhabela ferry town · Maresias surf beach

Half-day / overnight

If catching Ilhabela ferry

SP → São Sebastião

2h 30m drive

Ferry to Ilhabela

15 min · every 30 min · free for pedestrians

Worth stopping?

As gateway to Ilhabela, or for Maresias surf

Town character: A gateway more than a destination. Has a modest colonial historic center. Maresias Beach (within the municipality, 30 min south of town) is one of SP coast's most famous surf beaches with active nightlife and restaurants — a good half-day stop for surf-oriented travelers. Most visitors use São Sebastião as the embarkation point for Ilhabela.

SP State · Island · 15-min ferry

Ilhabela

Brazil's sailing capital · 360 waterfalls · Outstanding water clarity

2–3 nights

Minimum to justify the trip

SP → ferry terminal

2h 30m drive to São Sebastião

Ferry crossing

15 min · free for pedestrians · R$11–17 per car

Ferry frequency

Every 30 min (06:00–midnight) · hourly overnight

Car queue (high season)

Up to 1h — advance booking available (R$46–65)

Car needed on island?

For remote beaches yes; Centro walkable

Worth overnight?

Yes — 2 nights minimum

What makes it different: 85% of the island is protected Atlantic Forest State Park. This produces noticeably clearer water than the mainland SP coast — visibility difference is genuine. Brazil's established sailing capital with charter boats, regattas, and a sailing culture. 360+ waterfalls, some accessible by short hike.

Best beaches: Jabaquara (accessible from Centro, calm, family-friendly), Bonete (remote, spectacular, 3h hike or boat), Castelhanos (east coast, wild surf, 4WD required).

Waterfront/town: The Centro (Vila) has a walkable strip with restaurants, bars, and shops along the harbor — pleasant for evenings, lively during Carnival high season. Persistent mosquito warning: widely reported in reviews — DEET is essential.

SP State · 175 km from SP

Caraguatatuba

Mid-coast service hub · Pass-through

Functional city of ~130,000. Adequate beaches, budget-friendly. No distinctive cultural or scenic draw for international tourists. Serra do Mar hiking trails are the strongest nearby activity. Use as a fuel and lunch stop, not a tourist destination. No waterfront to speak of.

SP State · 220 km from SP

Ubatuba

102 beaches · Best beach variety on corridor · Car essential for beaches

2 nights + car

Recommended minimum

SP → Ubatuba

3h 30m drive via SP-099 / 5h bus

Ubatuba → Rio

4h 45m drive via Paraty

Car needed?

Yes for best beaches (10–30 km from town)

Uber?

Works but inconsistent — taxis more reliable

Town beach swimming

Not suitable — poor water quality in Itaguá

Worth overnight?

Yes — 2 nights with car

Best beaches: Vermelha do Norte (red-tinged sand, striking), Prumirim (calm, palm-lined, family), Félix (remote, crystalline, hiking access), Itamambuca (surf, long open beach), Saco da Ribeira (small harbour, sailing).

Waterfront/town: Itaguá district has a walkable evening strip (Rua Guarani) with family-run restaurants, informal fish-shack atmosphere, and local cachaça bars. Not a polished promenade but genuinely local and pleasant for dinner. The rest of the municipality is spread over 100 km — nothing is compact.

Key activity: Projeto TAMAR sea turtle conservation center (Praia Enseada) — interactive, worthwhile, accessible without a car.

RJ State · UNESCO WHS · Costa Verde

Paraty ★

Best overall stop · Colonial waterfront · No car needed in town

2 nights

Ideal visit

SP → Paraty

5h drive / 6h 30m bus

Paraty → Rio

3h 45m drive / 4h 30m–5h bus

Ferry / Boat

No ferry required to reach town

Car needed in town?

No — entire historic center is car-free

Car for beaches?

Helpful (Trindade 30 min) — taxis available

February special event

Bloco da Lama — unique mud Carnival parade

Waterfront — strongest on the entire corridor: The historic center is entirely car-free, stone-paved, and sits directly on a working fishing harbor with wooden wharfs and colorful fishing boats. Colonial buildings come to the waterline. Bay views frame forested mountains and islands. Evenings: candlelit restaurant terraces, live samba and bossa nova in open-front restaurants, artisan shops, cachaça tasting. This is the only destination on the corridor that delivers a complete tourist experience without requiring transport beyond walking.

Best beaches: Trindade (30 min by taxi or car — dramatic coastline, Pedra Que Engole rock pools), Praia do Sono (40 min + short hike), island beaches by boat tour from the harbor.

Activities: Historic center walk (3–4h), bay boat trip (half-day or full day, widely available), Trindade beach excursion, cachaça distillery visits, Bloco da Lama Carnival parade (February only).

February note: Wettest month (277–445mm rainfall). Rain is typically intense and brief — afternoons inside colonial cafés or pousadas are pleasant. Bloco da Lama draws large crowds during Carnival week; book accommodation months ahead.

RJ State · Costa Verde · 365 islands

Angra dos Reis

Bay of islands · Gateway to Ilha Grande · Boat-trip destination

1–2 nights

Best if boat-focused

SP → Angra

4h 30m drive / 7–8h bus

Angra → Rio

2h 20m drive / ~3h bus

Angra → Ilha Grande

30–40 min speedboat from Cais de Santa Luzia

Town waterfront?

Moderate — seafood restaurants, maritime feel

City appeal

Working city — value is on the water, not in town

Worth overnight?

Yes if combining with boat trips or Ilha Grande

Key distinction: 365 islands and 2,000+ beaches across Angra Bay — the payoff is almost entirely on the water. A half-day or full-day boat tour visits calm bay island beaches with turquoise water and no infrastructure. Without going on the water, the city itself is workaday rather than scenic. Best for travelers oriented toward boat trips, diving, and island exploration.

RJ State · Boat access only · No vehicles

Ilha Grande

Car-free island · Brazil's top beaches · Atlantic Forest hiking

2–3 nights

Minimum to justify logistics

Access

30–40 min speedboat from Angra dos Reis

Boat cost

~R$50–80 return per person

Vehicles on island?

None — sand paths and jungle trails only

Luggage warning

Wheeled suitcases are impractical — backpacks essential

Porter service

Carreteiro Legal (yellow shirts) at pier — licensed

Worth visiting?

Outstanding for backpack travelers · Complex for luggage-heavy

Best beaches: Lopes Mendes (consistently rated one of Brazil's top 5 beaches — powdery white sand, turquoise water, Atlantic Forest backdrop), Lagoa Azul (snorkeling lagoon), Praia Preta (black sand, dramatic).

Practical reality: This is an extraordinary destination but not a casual stop. The island has no roads, no cars, sand and cobbled paths throughout. International tourists with rolling suitcases will find arrival logistics genuinely awkward — licensed porters are available but suitcases still don't roll on sand paths between guesthouses. Ideal for backpacker-style travelers with 2–3 flexible nights. Not appropriate as a mid-route stop for standard-luggage tourists on a tight schedule.

RJ State · Costa Verde

Mangaratiba

Small coastal town · Ilha Grande alternative embarkation

Half-day / transit

Not a primary destination

Calm bay beaches (Sahy, Ibicuí, Muriqui), a small colonial waterfront with cafés and seafood restaurants, and the Emperor's Lookout panoramic viewpoint. More than a truck stop, considerably less than Paraty or Angra. Primary use: alternative Ilha Grande boat departure. Not worth a major detour as a standalone destination.

Direct Comparison: 8 Key Destinations

Santos · Guarujá · São Sebastião · Ilhabela · Ubatuba · Paraty · Angra dos Reis · Ilha Grande

Most traditional Brazilian beach city
Winner
Santos (working port city with deep beach culture) or Ubatuba (busy beach town with real local character and 102 beaches). Neither is a manufactured resort — both feel like places Brazilians actually live and use.
Best waterfront walking experience
Winner
Paraty — not close. Car-free colonial stones + fishing harbor + candlelit restaurants at waterline + evening live music. Santos is second for the Orla e Jardins scale (7km free promenade), but lacks Paraty's architectural character and atmosphere.
Most beautiful natural scenery
Winner
Ilha Grande (Atlantic Forest + exceptional beaches, no development) — closely followed by Ilhabela (360 waterfalls, clearest SP coast water, forested hills). Paraty's mountain-island-harbor composition from the historic center earns third place for total picture.
Best beach + town combination
Assessment
Paraty for quality of town + nearby beaches by boat/taxi. Ubatuba for quantity and quality of beaches + adequate town — but requires a car for beaches. Ilhabela comes third: island character + walkable Centro + spectacular beaches but car needed beyond Centro.
Most interesting historical experience
Winner
Paraty — UNESCO World Heritage listing (2019) for intact 18th-century colonial architecture functioning as a living town. São Sebastião has secondary colonial interest. Santos has port history and Museu Pelé. Nothing else on the corridor approaches Paraty historically.
Best for a short stop
Winner
Santos (half-day, no ferry, no car, proper tourist waterfront, 1h from SP). Paraty can be done as a 1-night stop but deserves more. Ilhabela and Ilha Grande are not practical short stops.
Requires more time
Assessment
Ilha Grande (2–3 nights minimum to justify logistics), Ilhabela (2–3 nights to reach remote beaches and waterfalls). Ubatuba also needs 2 nights with a car to be worthwhile. These three should not be attempted as quick stops.
Biggest transportation complication
Assessment
Ilha Grande — boat required, no vehicles on island, wheeled suitcases are a genuine practical problem. Ilhabela is simpler: free pedestrian ferry every 30 min, 15 min crossing. Angra is straightforward by car. Everything else is road-accessible.
Best overall tourist experience without requiring several days
Assessment
Paraty (2 nights) delivers the most complete and independent experience — walk everywhere in the historic center, boat trip from the harbor, excellent restaurants, no car required in town. Santos (half-day) is the most accessible single stop. These two serve different roles; they are not in competition.
Option 1 — 1 Day Available
São Paulo → Santos → Paraty → Rio · 2 days travel · 1 night stop
Day 1
08:00 Depart São Paulo (drive or Cometa bus from Jabaquara to Santos)
09:30 Arrive Santos · Orla e Jardins walk (7km garden promenade) · Museu Pelé or Monte Serrat tram
13:00 Depart Santos by car (bus requires a connection — car strongly recommended)
18:30 Arrive Paraty · Check in · Evening walk of car-free historic center · Dinner with live samba
Day 2
09:00 Morning walk of Paraty historic center · Breakfast at waterfront café
11:00 Optional: taxi to Trindade beach (30 min) or short boat trip
14:00 Depart Paraty by bus or car
17:45 Arrive Rio de Janeiro
Assessment
Manageable. Santos is a clean 3-hour morning stop. Paraty requires 5 hours from Santos by car. Total driving: ~7 hours across 2 days. Paraty feels slightly rushed at 1 night — the evening atmosphere is the highlight. Works as a minimum viable coastal stop.
Option 2 — 2 Days Available
São Paulo → Paraty (2 nights) → Rio
Day 1
09:00 Depart São Paulo by car
14:00 Arrive Paraty · Check in
14:00–18:00 First explore of car-free historic center · waterfront walk
18:00 Sunset at the harbor · Dinner in colonial center with live music
Day 2 (full day)
09:00 Boat tour of Paraty Bay — island beaches, snorkeling (~R$80–120/person, half-day)
13:00 Lunch in historic center
14:30 Taxi to Trindade Beach (30 min each way) — Pedra Que Engole rock pools
18:30 Return to Paraty · Dinner · Cachaça tasting · Evening walk
Day 3
09:00 Final walk, breakfast
10:30 Depart Paraty
14:15 Arrive Rio de Janeiro
Assessment
The right amount of time for Paraty. Two nights allow a boat trip and Trindade without rushing. Travel days are each ~4–5 hours but the destination fully justifies it. Recommended if Paraty is the priority and time is limited.
Option 3 — 3 Days Available
São Paulo → Ubatuba (1 night) → Paraty (2 nights) → Rio
Day 1
09:00 Depart São Paulo by car (SP-099 Tamoios highway)
12:30 Arrive Ubatuba · Projeto TAMAR turtle conservation center (2–3 hours)
15:00 Drive to Prumirim or Vermelha do Norte beach (20–30 min from town)
17:30 Return to Ubatuba · Rua Guarani dinner strip
20:00 Overnight Ubatuba
Day 2
08:30 Saco da Ribeira harbour · early morning beach
10:00 Drive south to Paraty (1 hour on BR-101)
11:00 Arrive Paraty · Check in · Historic center walk
15:00 Boat tour of the bay or afternoon rest
18:30 Sunset at harbor · Dinner with live music
Day 3 (full day Paraty)
09:00 Full-day boat trip — Ilha do Araújo, island beaches, snorkeling
13:30 Lunch on board or return to town
15:00 Trindade taxi excursion or afternoon walk
18:30 Final dinner in Paraty · Evening in colonial center
Day 4
08:00 Depart Paraty
11:45 Arrive Rio de Janeiro

Assessment: The most satisfying 3-day itinerary. Ubatuba provides the best beaches on the SP coast; Paraty provides the cultural and waterfront experience. No ferries required. Only a rental car. Total driving spread across 4 days is reasonable.

Geographic position of each destination. Each stop can be added or removed depending on available days.

   ↓ +1h drive from São Sebastião

Rio de Janeiro
Minimum viable coastal stop: Santos (half-day) + Paraty (2 nights) → Rio. No ferry, no rental car required in Paraty, most complete experience for the time invested.

February Conditions

Air temperature

28–32°C daily · rarely below 25°C at night

Sea temperature

26–27°C — ideal for swimming

Rainfall

Wettest month everywhere on this coast · heavy afternoon thunderstorms · Paraty 277–445mm

Rain pattern

Typically intense and brief (30–90 min) · mornings generally clear

Crowds

Peak season · Carnival week: prices 2–3× · book accommodation by December

Sea conditions

Calm in protected bays (Paraty, Angra) · strong surf on open beaches (Ubatuba, Maresias)

☔
Rain in February is not a trip-ruiner — it is usually brief and intense. Plan outdoor activities and beach visits for mornings. A light rain jacket packs flat and is worth bringing. Paraty's flooded colonial streets at high tide are photogenic, not dangerous. Ilha Grande trails are muddy in February — trail shoes recommended.

Rental Car vs. Public Transportation

Where a rental car transforms the experience
Ubatuba
Essential. Best beaches are 10–30 km from the town center. Without a car you're limited to Projeto TAMAR and the town strip. With a car, 102 beaches become accessible.
Ilhabela
Strongly recommended. Centro and Jabaquara are walkable, but remote beaches (Bonete, Castelhanos) require a 4WD or organized boat tour. No Uber on the island.
Paraty
Optional. The historic center is entirely walkable. Taxis are easily arranged for Trindade (R$40–60 return) and other beaches. Uber works for inter-city transfers.
Santos
Not needed. Bus from SP is cheap and fast. The Orla walk is self-contained. Excellent for a car-free half-day stop.
Ilha Grande
Useless. The island has no roads. Sand paths only. Leave the car in Angra.

Ferry and Boat Requirements

RouteRequired?DurationFrequencyCost (approx.)Complexity
Santos → GuarujáOptional10–15 minFrequentR$5 (foot)Very easy

Ilha Grande luggage warning: The island has no roads. Wheeled suitcases cannot be rolled on sand paths or cobblestones between the pier and guesthouses. Licensed porters (Carreteiro Legal, yellow shirts) are available at the pier — but suitcases still cannot roll between locations within the village. If you have standard rolling luggage, plan for this before booking Ilha Grande. Backpacks are the practical choice.

Safety

All destinations listed are considered tourist-safe relative to the Brazilian average. Standard urban precautions apply in Santos and Angra dos Reis city centers. Paraty's car-free historic center is relaxed and low-crime in tourist areas. Ilha Grande's Vila do Abraão is calm. Remote trails on Ilha Grande should not be walked alone at night. In all beach towns: do not leave valuables unattended on the beach during Carnival week when crowds are large.

Key confirmations: Camarote Mar · Feb 9 · Sector 6 ✓ confirmed  ·  Late Airbnb checkout Feb 10 — arrange with host at booking  ·  GIG → IGU evening flight — book when 2027 schedules publish (~Oct 2026)  ·  Macuco Safari Feb 11 — sells out in February, book early
📅

Feb 6–14 at a glance: 9 days across Rio + Iguazu. Feb 5: depart JFK 10:00 PM → Buenos Aires (overnight). Rio (Feb 6–10): Four nights at the Copacabana Airbnb (R. Santa Clara, 405). Land GIG 3:40 PM on Feb 6. Sightseeing Feb 6, 7, 8. Carnival night Feb 9. Recovery + evening flight to Iguazu Feb 10. Iguazu (Feb 10–14): Four nights at Sanma Hotel by Nobile, near the Brazilian park. Brazilian side + Macuco Safari Feb 11. Argentine side Feb 12. Free day Feb 13 (Yup Star + Triple Frontier evening; Rafain dinner show kept as backup). Fly home Feb 14 (IGU → GRU → JFK, land Feb 15 7:05 AM). Rio Airbnb is the geographic reference for all Rio distances.

Friday, Feb 5 — Depart New York (JFK)
Overnight flight via Buenos Aires · The trip begins
Evening
10:00 PM — depart JFK → Buenos Aires (EZE). Overnight flight (~10.5 hrs). Check in 3 hrs early; eat before or after boarding.
Group
Fly tonight (JFK 10:00 PM → Buenos Aires, overnight). Anyone on the São Paulo pre-Carnival leg (Jan 29–Feb 5, see the São Paulo tab) meets in Rio on Feb 6.
Night
Overnight flight. Land EZE 10:45 AM Saturday.
Saturday, Feb 6 — Arrival
Settle in · First evening
Context
Série Ouro parades at Sambadrome tonight (second-division schools). Major blocos citywide. Some road disruptions expected near parade routes.
Arrival
Land Buenos Aires (EZE) 10:45 AM → connect 12:45 PM. Two-hour connection — move fast, follow transit signs. Land Rio (GIG) 3:40 PM. Transfer to the Copacabana Airbnb, R. Santa Clara 405 (~45–60 min). Settle in; walk the promenade to orient; pão de queijo + café from a padaria nearby. Anyone arriving from the São Paulo leg joins here — confirm arrival timing separately.
Evening
~5:00 PM: arrive and settle at the Airbnb — freshen up, change out of travel clothes, wifi, message home; 30 minutes, no more. 5:30–6:00 PM: promenade walk toward Arpoador (~1.4 km, ~15 min) with a padaria stop for pão de queijo + café. ~6:45 PM: sunset at Arpoador Rock — the crowd applauds when the sun drops; free and genuinely Rio. 7:30–8:30 PM: light dinner — Ipanema (10–15 min walk from Arpoador, livelier, more vegetarian-friendly kitchens) or back in Copacabana. ~10:00 PM: early night; unpack and lay out tomorrow's kit. Confirm the São Paulo → Rio arrival timing tonight or tomorrow morning.
Distance
Arpoador from Airbnb: ~1.4 km / approx 15 min walk via Copacabana Beach boardwalk.
Sunday, Feb 7 — Full Rio Day
Cristo · Santa Teresa · Bloco evening
6:30 AM
Weather check — the day's most important decision. Look at the sky over Corcovado from the window and check a weather app. If the summit is clear, proceed with Cristo at 8 AM as planned; if heavily clouded or raining, start with Santa Teresa/Selarón/Lapa instead. Never go up Corcovado in cloud — the view will be zero.
6:45 AM
Breakfast near the Airbnb. Grab-and-go from a padaria or café within 5 minutes of R. Santa Clara, 405 — pão de queijo with café com leite, or tapioca with cheese and juice. Keep it fast; you must depart by 7:30 AM. No sit-down breakfast this morning.
7:30 AM
Depart Airbnb → Cosme Velho. Uber ~25–35 minutes in Carnival traffic (~7 km). Request the Uber from an interior street like Rua Barata Ribeiro — never from Av. Atlântica during bloco hours. Destination: Rua Cosme Velho, 513, the Trem do Corcovado station. Budget R$40–70 with surge.
8:00–10:30 AM
Cristo Redentor. Timed tram tickets must be bought online in advance at tremdocorcovado.rio — the 8 AM first train sells out in Carnival week, so book before leaving home. The tram climbs ~20 minutes to the 709 m summit; spend 1.5–2 hours walking the full terrace. On a clear morning you can see Maracanã, the Sambadrome, and all of Guanabara Bay.
10:45–11:30 AM
Mirante Dona Marta. Free viewpoint at 355 m, on the natural route from Cosme Velho toward Santa Teresa (~3 km, 10–15 min Uber). Cristo framed above on the right, the bay panorama below — the classic "Cristo from below" shot. 30–45 minutes is enough; no ticket, no booking.
11:45 AM–1:30 PM
Santa Teresa wander + lunch. Rio's bohemian hillside: cobblestone streets, street art, colonial houses. Walk the Largo do Guimarães → Largo das Neves axis with no fixed plan. Lunch: Aprazível (Rua Aprazível, 62 — terrace with jungle views, mains R$70–120) or the simpler Bar do Mineiro (Rua Paschoal Carlos Magno, 99 — classic boteco, cash preferred). Allow ~2 hours combined.
2:00–2:45 PM
Escadaria Selarón. Walk downhill from Santa Teresa (20–30 min on cobblestones via Rua Joaquim Murtinho) or take a 5-min Uber to Rua Joaquim Silva. 215 steps covered in 2,000+ tiles from 60+ countries — photograph from the bottom looking up and find tiles from your own country. Free; arrive before 3 PM to beat the Sunday crowds. Wear grip shoes.
2:45–4:00 PM
Lapa Arches + café pause. 10-minute walk from the base of the steps to the Arcos da Lapa, the 18th-century aqueduct — quiet and photogenic by day. Rest at a juice bar and hydrate; it's midday heat. Then Uber back to the Airbnb (~15–20 min, ~8 km).
4:00–4:30 PM
Airbnb rest & change. Short, non-negotiable rest: shower, change into light bloco clothes, drink water, eat a snack. Pack light for the street party — phone, some cash, water, minimal valuables. Agree on a group meeting point in case anyone gets separated.
4:30–7:00 PM
Bloco: Simpatia é Quase Amor (Ipanema). The target — the best Carnival-Sunday bloco, traditionally parading on this day, 100,000+ people of pure joy, ~15–20 min from the Airbnb. Confirm its 2027 parade day and meeting point on carnavalderua.rio (published ~Dec/Jan) before the trip. Since it's beachside, you'll catch the ~6:45 PM sunset from the sand — no separate Arpoador trip needed.
7:30–8:30 PM
Dinner. Keep it simple after a full day on your feet — eat near where the bloco ended, or walk back toward Copacabana for padarias and juice bars near the Airbnb. Light, vegetarian-friendly, early.
~10:00 PM
Return to the Airbnb. Every night ends at R. Santa Clara, 405. Unpack the day bag, lay out tomorrow's kit, sleep — Feb 8 starts at 7 AM for Sargento Pimenta.
Note
No Sambadrome tonight — our confirmed night is Feb 9 only.
Monday, Feb 8 — Carnival Monday: Bloco + Sugarloaf
Sargento Pimenta · Pão de Açúcar · Arpoador sunset
6:30 AM
Wake up, breakfast near the Airbnb. Quick padaria breakfast within 5 minutes of R. Santa Clara, 405 — coffee and pão de queijo. Keep it fast; you depart at 7:00 AM. You'll eat again at the bloco — food vendors are everywhere at Aterro.
7:00 AM
Depart Airbnb → Aterro do Flamengo. Take the metro, not an Uber — Carnival Monday brings severe road closures around Flamengo. Walk ~8 min to Siqueira Campos station → Line 1 to Catete (~10 min) → walk ~8–10 min to the park entrance. Fare ~R$5–8. Arrive by 7:50 AM.
8:00 AM–1:30 PM
Sargento Pimenta bloco. The Carnival Monday tradition since the 1990s: a full marching band playing the Beatles' entire catalog as carnival marchinhas — "Yesterday" as samba, "Let It Be" as pagode. Hundreds of thousands gather in the open bay-side park with Sugarloaf as the backdrop. Stay 3–5 hours, as long as energy holds. Bring water; wear clothes you don't mind getting sweaty. (2027 schedule unconfirmed — verify on carnaval.rio / Riotur app in January 2027.)
1:30 PM
Aterro → Sugarloaf. Taxi/Uber from inside the park to Praça General Tibúrcio, Praia Vermelha — the cable car base. Only ~4 km, 5–7 min, R$20–35. This is the most natural geographic pairing of the whole week. Grab a quick snack at the base if needed.
2:00–5:30 PM
Sugarloaf Mountain (Pão de Açúcar). Cable car runs 8 AM–9 PM in two stages: first to Morro da Urca (212 m, restaurant + panoramic walkway), then to the Sugarloaf summit (396 m). Spend time on BOTH levels — Urca gives the city panorama, the summit gives the bay panorama with Cristo above. Afternoon timing is ideal: golden light from ~4 PM turns the bay copper. No advance booking needed; buy at the booth (~R$150–170/person, 2026 price — recheck). The 2 PM arrival beats the Carnival-week morning rush.
5:30 PM
Sugarloaf → Airbnb. Uber back to Copacabana (~7 km, 20–25 min in Carnival Monday traffic, R$30–50 surge). Rest, shower, change. Tonight stays moderate — tomorrow is Camarote Mar and you need full stamina until dawn.
6:15 PM
Arpoador sunset (optional, if energy remains). 15-minute walk from the Airbnb to the rock; sunset is 6:36 PM on Feb 8. Genuinely optional — the bloco + Sugarloaf is already a full day. Skip guilt-free if tired.
7:30 PM
Dinner near the Airbnb. Keep it close — Copacabana has plenty within a 5-minute walk. Light-to-moderate, vegetarian-friendly. No excess tonight; tomorrow requires stamina until dawn.
9:00–9:30 PM
Return to the Airbnb. Back at R. Santa Clara, 405 by 9:30 PM, lights out by 10 PM. Tomorrow: sleep in, no alarm — rest day before Camarote Mar.
Note
No Sambadrome tonight — our only night is Feb 9.
Tuesday, Feb 9 — CAMAROTE MAR ✓
Special Group Night 3 · Final night · Our confirmed booking
8:00 AM
Wake up, no alarm. Sleep in. Light padaria breakfast near the Airbnb — pão de queijo, fruit, coffee or açaí. Today is deliberately low-effort: the night is the main event, and you'll be up until ~4–5 AM.
8:45 AM–12:30 PM
Urca + Praia Vermelha (morning only). Uber ~10–15 min (~3.7 km) from Rua Barata Ribeiro. Walk the Pista Cláudio Coutinho forest trail at the base of Sugarloaf, beach time at the small sheltered cove of Praia Vermelha, then the Mureta da Urca locals' waterfront scene. Back at the Airbnb by 12:30 PM. Low-effort, genuinely Rio, nothing like the other days.
Backup
Morning backup: Jardim Botânico + Parque Lage (instead of Urca). The two remaining top-10 sights sit ~10 min apart and are equally low-effort: 8:45 AM Uber (~20–25 min) → 9:15–10:15 AM Parque Lage (free, opens 9 AM — 1920s mansion, courtyard pool, Cristo towering above) → 10:30 AM–12:00 PM Jardim Botânico (opens 8 AM on Tuesdays — royal palm avenue, orchid house, lakes, monkeys; ~R$75–80/person, book tickets online in advance) → Uber back by 12:30 PM. Shady, flat, calm — arguably even better rest before the Sambadrome night. Pick this if you want to complete all 10 top sights; keep Urca if you prefer the beach-trail-local morning.
~1:00 PM
Lunch near the Airbnb. Comida a quilo — rice, verified vegetarian beans, grilled vegetables, salad. Eat well; this is your fuel for the night.
1:30–3:30 PM
Protected rest. Nap, hydrate, stay off your feet. Non-negotiable.
3:30–5:00 PM
Shower and prepare. Lay out the night kit: your Camarote Mar credential and the mandatory official T-shirt (collected at credentialing — check your booking docs for when/where; it's required for entry), phone, some cash/card, a light layer. Dress code is elegant-casual with Carnival flair. Minimal valuables.
~5:30 PM
Early dinner near the Airbnb. Light — you won't eat a full meal again until the camarote's buffet. Hydrate.
Meeting time − 10 min
Walk to Othon Palace. ~300 m / 3–5 min along the beachfront from R. Santa Clara, 405 to Av. Atlântica, 3264. Confirm the exact meeting time from your booking documentation (camarote transfers typically depart ~7–8 PM for a ~9:30 PM parade start) and be there 10 minutes early.
Transport
Round-trip transfers between the Othon Palace meeting point and the Sambadrome are INCLUDED in your Camarote Mar ticket (per Camarote Mar's official site). After the final parade, return transfers run from the designated pickup area back to Othon Palace — then the 5-min walk to the Airbnb. Fallback if ever needed: Metro Line 2 from Praça Onze (runs 24h on parade nights) → transfer at Central → Siqueira Campos → 8-min walk.
~9:30 PM–~3 AM
Special Group Night 3, Sector 6. The final parade night: 4 top samba schools, each with jaw-dropping floats, thousands of costumed paraders, and 250+ percussionists in the drum section. Sector 6 is central — near the judges' tables, where schools perform at their peak. Between schools, the camarote runs its own party: live Brazilian artists and DJs across multiple floors. Inside: premium open bar all night (Grey Goose, Bombay Sapphire, Chandon, Dewar's 12, beer, signature cocktails), curated Brazilian/international buffet stations running late, ~3,000 guests, climate-controlled lounges.
~3:30–5:00 AM (Feb 10)
Return. Included return transfer from the Sambadrome pickup area back to Othon Palace, then the 5-minute walk to the Airbnb. In bed by ~5 AM. Checkout isn't until ~1 PM — you've earned the sleep.
Note
Verify two things from your booking docs before the trip: the exact Othon Palace meeting time and the credentialing details (when/where you collect the ticket + mandatory T-shirt).
Wednesday, Feb 10 — Recovery + Fly to Iguazu
Post-Carnival · Ash Wednesday · Late wake · Pack · Checkout · GIG → Foz · Hotel Night 1
~5:00 AM
Back from the Sambadrome. Included Camarote Mar return transfer to Othon Palace, then the 5-minute walk to the Airbnb at R. Santa Clara, 405. Straight to sleep — checkout isn't until ~1 PM. Earplugs + eye mask: Ash Wednesday morning blocos in Copacabana are loud, and you'll be sleeping through them.
12:00 PM
Soft alarm, brunch. Short morning by design. Brunch at or within 5 minutes of the apartment — padaria, juice bar. Hydrate well; last night was a long one. Traffic check: look at Waze/Google Maps for Linha Vermelha conditions, and check the official 2027 bloco calendar (released January 2027) for any Ash Wednesday blocos near Copacabana that could close streets around the apartment.
1:00–1:30 PM
Final pack + checkout, R. Santa Clara, 405. Packing should ideally be finished before Carnival night — this is just the final zip-up. Bags at the door by 1:15 PM; check out by 1:30 PM sharp. No late checkout works with a 4:25 PM flight.
~1:15–1:30 PM
Depart for GIG Terminal 2. Uber ~45–55 min via Túnel Rebouças → Linha Vermelha — this route avoids the Sambadrome/Apoteose/Central zone entirely (the Apuração results chaos is Wednesday afternoon, but it's not on your route). Request pickup from Rua Barata Ribeiro (interior street), never Av. Atlântica — Ash Wednesday blocos can close the waterfront with no notice; have a backup pickup point one block over. Leave at 1:15 PM if traffic is red; 1:30 PM at the latest. Reversible lanes are suspended during Carnival, so assume slower traffic. Expect surge pricing — have a card ready in the app and don't waste time comparing apps.
2:30–4:25 PM
GIG Terminal 2. Do GOL online check-in 48h before departure (opens ~4:25 PM on Feb 8 — you can do it from the Airbnb; GOL's window is 48h to 1h before the flight). Ash Wednesday is mass-exodus day — expect long bag-drop lines. Be at the airport by 2:30 PM; domestic bag drop closes ~40 min before departure, so the 2-hour buffer is intentional, not generous. Grab a snack; Terminal 2 has decent food options.
4:25 PM
GOL G3 1866 — GIG Terminal 2 → IGU (Foz do Iguaçu / Cataratas International Airport). Direct 2h15m, Boeing 737-800. Seats: Rahul Maheshwari 07A, Priti Maheshwari 07B, Manish Kumar 07C, Kirti Jindal 06C. Do NOT fly to IGR (Puerto Iguazú, Argentina) — no direct flights from Rio; IGU is the only practical option.
6:40 PM
Land at IGU. Small airport, domestic arrival — no immigration, no passport control. Deplane and baggage claim take ~15–20 min. ATMs and the taxi stand are in arrivals if you need cash.
~7:00 PM
IGU → Sanma Hotel (~20–25 min). Pre-booked private transfer is recommended — arrange before the trip so the driver is waiting with your name. Alternatives: Uber X (~R$35) or taxi (~R$70) — 2026 approx prices, recheck closer to the trip. Hotel: Rodovia das Cataratas, Km 21 — ~0.5 km from the Brazilian falls entrance, 235 m from Parque das Aves.
~7:15 PM
Check in at Sanma Hotel by Nobile. Check-in runs from 3 PM, so 7:15 PM is no issue. Four nights, Feb 10–14, breakfast included. At the desk: confirm breakfast hours (6:30–10:30 AM, Restaurante Amaru) and WiFi. Unpack properly — you're here four nights.
~8:00 PM
Buy Feb 11 tickets online — do it tonight. Brazilian park entry ~R$134/adult (2026 foreigner price) at tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br + Macuco Safari ~R$386/person (2026 range R$350–400) at macucosafari.com.br. Both QRs on your phone = zero ticket lines tomorrow morning. Optional Parque das Aves ~R$80, buy at the door — 2026 price, recheck in 2027.
~8:30 PM
Light dinner, sleep. Hotel restaurant or nearby — keep it light after the travel day. Early night: tomorrow starts at 7 AM for the Brazilian side, the biggest single day of the Iguazu portion.
Note
The Apuração (official Carnival results, announced Wednesday afternoon at the Sambadrome) happens while you're at the airport — follow it on the news if you're curious.
Thursday, Feb 11 — Brazilian Side (Full Day)
Parque Nacional do Iguaçu · Trilha das Cataratas · Macuco Safari · Devil's Throat decks · from Sanma Hotel
Tickets (buy Feb 10 night)
Park entry — tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br, ~R$134/adult (foreigner rate). Date-specific; enter any time during opening hours. Macuco Safari — macucosafari.com.br, ~R$386/person (2026 figure — recheck for 2027). No time slot: boats depart every ~15–20 min from 9:00 AM. Park admission is not included in the Macuco price — you need both tickets. Parque das Aves (optional) — ~R$80, buy at the door. Total ≈ R$600. Buying online the night before means zero ticket lines in the morning.
Pack
Swimsuit or quick-dry clothes + sandals (boat), full change of dry clothes, plastic bag for wet gear, waterproof phone pouch, ≥1.5 L water, trail snacks, DEET, sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, small towel, R$300–500 cash + Visa. Leave passport in the hotel safe — no border crossing today.
7:00 AM
Wake up at Sanma. Full park day — the biggest single day of the Iguazu portion. No border crossing: both hotel and park are in Brazil, so the passport stays in the hotel safe. The park opens at 9:00 AM on weekdays (last entry 4:00 PM); arriving early beats the midday crowds and the worst of the February heat.
7:30 AM
Breakfast at Sanma (included). Brazilian hotel breakfasts are a vegetarian's dream — tropical fruits, breads, cheeses, eggs, tapioca, cakes. Eat a proper meal: you will walk several kilometres in February humidity and get soaked by mid-morning. Drink plenty of water, apply sunscreen now, and fill your water bottles — there is nothing to drink between the trailhead and lunch.
8:20 AM
Leave Sanma on foot. The park entrance is an 8-minute walk along Rodovia das Cataratas — flat, straightforward, no Uber needed. Daypack check: swimsuit/quick-dry clothes on or packed, full change of clothes, plastic bag for wet gear, waterproof phone pouch, DEET, hat, water, snacks, cash + card.
8:30 AM
At the visitor-center turnstiles. The Centro de Visitantes: turnstiles, shops, restrooms, café. Show your online QR and walk straight through — no ticket line. The park opens at 9:00 AM, so you are near the front of the line on a peak-season February morning. Use the restrooms here; the next facilities are at the Macuco dock.
9:00 AM
First park shuttle bus to Stop 1. Private cars cannot enter the park — everyone rides the included buses, every ~10–15 min, three hop-on/hop-off stops, no separate fare or reservation. Ride to Stop 1: the Macuco Safari dock.
9:15–11:15 AM
Macuco Safari (~2 hrs, three stages). ① 3 km open-cart jungle ride through Atlantic rainforest with a bilingual guide. ② 600 m suspended forest walkway to the base deck — lockers, restrooms, snack bar; stash dry clothes here. ③ Twin-engine boats up the river through rapids, driven directly under the cascades. Life jackets provided; the operator runs under a federal concession with Inmetro/ABNT safety certification. You will be completely soaked — that is the point.

Tickets — two required, bought separately: ① Park admission ~R$134/adult (foreigner rate) at tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br. ② Macuco Safari ticket ~R$386/person at macucosafari.com.br (official site). The Macuco price does not include park entry. Book both online on Feb 10 night — do not buy at the dock in February. Peak-season days sell out, and pre-booked visitors get priority boarding; buying at the dock is possible but risks sellout plus a second queue. With both QRs on your phone the morning is frictionless: turnstiles (no line) → shuttle → Stop 1 → straight into the next departing group. Even pre-booked, expect a short boarding wait — the 9:00 AM first departures keep it minimal, while later in the day waits can stretch past an hour. (A private no-queue option exists at R$597/person with towels, raincoats, drinks and lunch box — but it needs 4+ paying adults and a prior appointment.)
11:15–11:30 AM
Change into dry clothes at the dock deck's restrooms and lockers. Wet gear goes into the zip bag — you are dry for the rest of the day. Snack bar and souvenir shop at the deck while you regroup.
11:30 AM
Shuttle to Stop 2: Trilha das Cataratas trailhead. Short ride. Use the restrooms here — the trail is effectively one-way with no facilities until the end at Porto Canoas.
11:45 AM–1:15 PM
Trilha das Cataratas (1.2 km, ~90 min). Paved, mostly flat trail with frontal viewpoints across the gorge — the only place all ~275 falls appear in one panorama. Coatis roam the trail (don't feed them). Finale: the metal walkway jutting over the river directly in front of the Devil's Throat — deafening, mist-soaked, rainbows — then the panoramic glass elevator to the top deck.
1:15–2:15 PM
Lunch at Porto Canoas (trail's end, open 12:00–4:00 PM). Buffet with river views, confirmed vegetarian-friendly with plenty of vegan options. Caution: black beans are often cooked with pork and farofa may contain bacon — ask staff before serving. Drinks and desserts extra. Rest your legs — you have earned it.
2:15–2:45 PM
Upper deck & Espaço Naipi. Final panoramic photos with the full sweep of the falls from above, plus a gift shop for souvenirs. The classic postcard angle — the wide shot of the entire system you cannot get anywhere else.
3:00–4:15 PM
Optional: Parque das Aves. Bird park beside the park entrance (~4 min walk from Sanma): 150+ species — toucans, macaws, flamingos — in walk-through aviaries. ~R$80, ~1.5 hrs, no booking, vegetarian-friendly café. Skip guilt-free if tired. Note: take the park shuttle back to the visitor center first, then walk to the bird park entrance.
4:30 PM
Last return shuttle from Stop 3 — do not miss it. The park day ends at 5:00 PM; this bus carries you back to the visitor center. Be at the stop with time to spare. (If you did Parque das Aves, you are already at the entrance.)
5:00–5:15 PM
Walk back to Sanma (8 min). Shower, rest 60–90 min. Confirm tomorrow's Argentine-side transfer at the front desk if you have not already.
Evening
Rest at the hotel — early night. Light dinner near Sanma; the Rafain Show moved to Feb 13 (backup option). Pack tomorrow's daypack tonight: same kit minus the swimsuit, broken-in walking shoes, and passport in the bag — Friday means a border crossing, with 45–90 min of formalities before you reach the Argentine park. 6:00 AM wake.
Night-before (Feb 10)
☐ Park ticket online (tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br), QR downloaded offline · ☐ Macuco Safari ticket (macucosafari.com.br) · ☐ Confirm Feb 12 Argentine transfer at Sanma's front desk · ☐ Pack daypack per the list above · ☐ Notify bank of Brazil/Argentina travel dates.
Money
International Visa works everywhere that matters (park, Macuco, restaurants, Uber). Carry R$300–500 cash for kiosks, small vendors, taxis. Always pay in reais (BRL), never USD, at card terminals.
Friday, Feb 12 — Full Day Iguazu: Argentine Side
Border crossing · Parque Nacional Iguazú · Garganta del Diablo · Lower + Upper Circuits
⚠️ Status check (do in Jan 2027)
As of September 2026, the Devil's Throat walkway on the Argentine side is temporarily closed — sections were removed as a precaution against unusually high river levels. Your trip is February 2027, so check the park's official channels in January 2027. If it is still closed, the day still works: reallocate the morning to the Lower and Upper circuits, which together are a full day on their own. Everything below assumes it has reopened.
Tickets (buy in advance)
Argentine park admission — buy online in advance at ventaweb.apn.gob.ar (the official National Parks portal; tickets are not reliably sold at the gate). Roughly ARS 35,000–45,000 per foreign adult (2026 figures — Argentine prices move fast, recheck for 2027; about USD 26–35). The ticket includes the Ecological Train and all three circuits. Screenshot the QR offline. Park opens 8:00 AM daily. Note: some travelers report buying at the gate works — but in February peak season, online is the safe play. Note: the Gran Aventura boat ride (~USD 110–150, not included in the park ticket) is deliberately skipped — the Macuco Safari boat on Feb 11 already covers the under-the-falls experience, and the boat would force dropping the Upper Circuit. This day keeps all three walking circuits: Devil's Throat + Lower + Upper.
Transport (arrange Feb 11 night)
Do NOT rely on Uber — Uber does not quote cross-border trips and drivers routinely refuse them. Arrange a taxi, remise (private car), or hotel transfer at Sanma's front desk the night before: agree a fixed round-trip price in advance, with 7:00 AM pickup and the driver waiting through both immigration posts and the ~7-hour park visit. Cross-border taxi drivers do this run daily — the driver hands you the Argentine entry form to fill in transit, tells you exactly where to go at each post, and waits. You (not the driver) must get out with your passport at each post — that is the law, no exceptions. Agree the price before getting in.
Pack
Passport — physical, in hand, in an easily reachable pocket. It is the single most important item today: four immigration posts, no passport, no crossing. Also: park ticket QR (screenshot offline), ≥1.5 L water, snacks, sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, DEET, poncho/rain shell, waterproof phone pouch, small towel, cash in reais for the taxi (card works at the park and restaurants). Broken-in walking shoes — 6–8 km of walking today, and the Lower Circuit has steep wet stairs. No swimsuit needed (no boat planned on this side).
6:00 AM
Wake up at Sanma. This schedule puts you at the Argentine park around 8:30 AM — on one of the first Ecological Trains to Devil's Throat, still well ahead of the tour-bus crowds. Lay out the daypack the night-before way — passport in an easily reachable pocket, not buried. Hydrate early.
6:30–7:00 AM
Breakfast at Restaurante Amaru — a full, unhurried 30 minutes. The buffet opens at 6:30 AM sharp (served daily 6:30–10:30 AM, included in your rate — verified). Fresh fruit, breads, and the made-to-order station (tapioca, eggs — vegetarian-friendly). You will not sit down for lunch until ~11:15, and the morning is immigration lines plus the Devil's Throat walkway, so eat properly. Fill water bottles; apply sunscreen and DEET before leaving.
7:00 AM
Meet your driver in the lobby — depart. Confirm the fixed round-trip price one more time before getting in, and confirm the waiting arrangement and pickup meeting point at the Argentine park (~7 hours later). Drive ~15 min to the Brazilian Polícia Federal post via Av. das Cataratas. At 7:00 AM the roads and the border are still quiet — the tour buses head out later.
~7:15 AM — Brazilian exit
First immigration stop: Polícia Federal (Brazilian exit). Get out with your passport — the driver waits with the car. Join the exit line, present your passport, receive the exit stamp. At this hour it is usually 10–15 minutes. (Some day-trippers skip this post since they return the same evening — do not. You need a clean re-entry stamp when you fly out of IGU on Feb 14, and the stop costs ten minutes.)
~7:30 AM — The bridge
Cross the Ponte Tancredo Neves over the Iguaçu River — the actual country line is mid-bridge, about five minutes of driving. Have your passport and the Argentine entry form (your driver usually hands it to you in transit — fill it in the car) ready.
~7:40 AM — Argentine entry
Second immigration stop: Dirección Nacional de Migraciones (Argentine entry). Get out with your passport and completed entry form. Queue, present documents and answer the standard questions (where are you staying? how long?). Whether you receive a stamp or slip depends on nationality and current procedures — keep whatever they give you. Before 8:00 AM you are still ahead of the tour-bus wave: typically 15–25 minutes at this hour, versus 45+ later in the morning. Your driver waits; agree beforehand where he will park. Total hotel-to-park time: ~80–95 minutes.
~8:05–8:25 AM — To the park
Drive ~20 min from the border to the Parque Nacional Iguazú entrance (past Puerto Iguazú town). Use the restrooms at the visitor center before entering. Show your pre-bought QR — no ticket line. Collect a park map. You are arriving within half an hour of the 8:00 AM opening — still among the first visitors of the day.
8:25–8:40 AM — Enter the park
Through the turnstiles with your QR. Head straight for Estación Central — the Ecological Train departure point. You will likely catch the second train to Garganta station (~8:50 AM) — Devil's Throat first is the entire strategy: smallest crowds, best light, shortest train queues.
~8:50 AM — Eco-train
Open-air Ecological Train through the rainforest to Garganta station (~20 min ride, included in your ticket). The track cuts through dense Atlantic Forest canopy — keep the camera ready for toucans, monkeys, and coatis along the way. This is the only motorized transport inside the park; everything else is on foot.
9:20–10:20 AM — Devil's Throat
Garganta del Diablo — the centerpiece of Iguazu, both sides, any season. From the station, a 1.1 km flat elevated catwalk crosses the upper Iguaçu River — the river fans into dozens of channels across the floodplain before dropping simultaneously into the gorge, and you hear it long before you see it. The platform sits directly above the horseshoe-shaped chasm — note the catwalk has closed for repairs in past years, so recheck Devil's Throat access status shortly before travel (82 m deep, 150 m wide) where half the river's flow plunges at once. In February, peak water volume, the falls dissolve into white thunder and the roar is physical. The spray is total — poncho on, phone in the waterproof pouch. You are still well ahead of the midday crowds. Allow up to 45 minutes at the platform; walk the catwalk back to the station. (If the walkway is still closed from the 2026 high-water works, reallocate this block: extend the Lower Circuit and add the Argentine Macuco jungle trail.)
10:35–11:05 AM — Train back
Eco-train back to Estación Cataratas (the middle station, ~15 min). Restrooms, water refill, regroup. You are now switching from the panoramic morning to the immersive afternoon.
11:15 AM–12:15 PM — Lunch
Lunch at the park's main restaurant complex near Estación Cataratas — still ahead of the worst of the noon rush. Full restaurants and snack bars; vegetarian options are usually available — empanadas de verdura, pasta, salads — but ask about meat stock (¿Tiene caldo de carne?) the way you would ask about pork in Brazil. Rest your legs properly: the afternoon is ~3.5 km of walking with stairs.
12:30–2:30 PM — Lower Circuit
Circuito Inferior (~1.7 km, ~2 hrs, many stairs). The most immersive circuit in the park: the trail descends into the gorge and runs along the base of multiple falls at water level — you feel the falls rather than just seeing them, including the viewpoint at the boat dock facing the cascades head-on. This is the wettest and most physically demanding section: steep descents and ascents, slippery surfaces, sturdy shoes essential. Coatis, butterflies, and rainbows in the spray everywhere.
2:45–4:00 PM — Upper Circuit
