Circuito Superior (~1.4–1.9 km, ~1–1.5 hrs, mostly flat elevated walkway). The panoramic circuit: you walk along the top of the falls looking down the drop line of the major cascades, with the jungle canopy and the canyon spreading below — the wide-angle complement to the morning's close-ups. Calmer, drier, and the gentlest walking of the three circuits. Done by ~4:00 PM, before the falls areas begin closing.
4:00–4:30 PM — Exit, meet driver
Walk out to the park entrance and meet your driver at the agreed spot. Restrooms, water, final souvenir check. Confirm the return route — same two posts in reverse.
4:30–5:30 PM — Border back
Reverse the morning: Argentine exit stamp, bridge, Brazilian entry stamp. Same drill — you get out with your passport at each post, the driver waits. Late-afternoon crossings are typically faster than morning ones, but Friday traffic can bunch up; budget up to an hour. The Brazilian re-entry stamp is the one that matters for your Feb 14 flight out of IGU — make sure you get it.
5:45–6:00 PM — Sanma
Back at the hotel. Shower, feet up. You walked 6–8 km across two countries today — take a proper rest before dinner. The hardest day of the Iguazu portion is behind you.
7:00 PM — Dinner
Dinner near the hotel or in Foz. Tomorrow (Feb 13) is your free day: no alarm, no border, no schedule. Eat well; you have earned it.
9:30 PM — Rest
Lights out. Optional: sketch your Feb 13 free-day plan — Itaipu Dam, Parque das Aves (if you skipped it on Feb 11), Puerto Iguazú town, or a genuine rest day by the pool. No tickets to buy tonight, no early alarm tomorrow.
Saturday, Feb 13 — Free Day in Foz
No alarm · Bird Park · Itaipu Dam · Yup Star + Triple Frontier evening · Rafain (backup)
Morning
No alarm — sleep in. Relaxed breakfast at Sanma. Two huge falls days are behind you; today moves at your pace.
10:00 AM–12:30 PM
Parque das Aves (Bird Park). 4-min walk from Sanma (~R$110 at the door, 2026 prices), 2–3 hrs. Walk-through aviaries — toucans, macaws, parrots. No booking needed.
12:30–1:30 PM
Lunch at or near the hotel.
2:00–5:00 PM
Itaipu Dam panoramic tour. Book via the hotel front desk; hotel-pickup tours ~USD 35–40 (2026 prices). The special behind-the-scenes tour (~R$182) goes inside the dam if you want the deeper version. ~3 hrs with transfers.
5:30–6:15 PM
Yup Star Ferris wheel at sunset. 88m high with air-conditioned cabins, ~20-min ride, 360° views over the triple-border region where the Iguaçu and Paraná rivers meet (~R$60–79, open daily 12:30–8:30 PM). The standout moment of the day — right by the Marco complex.
6:30–8:30 PM
Marco das Três Fronteiras. Where Brazil, Argentina, and Paraguay meet. Entry ~R$55–60; cultural show ~6:30 PM; dinner at the Cabeza de Vaca restaurant inside the complex. Back at Sanma ~9 PM. Skip without guilt if you'd rather rest — pool and spa are the fallback.
Alternative
Guarani Village cultural visit instead of the dam, or a pure rest day — your call.
7:00–11:00 PM (backup)
Rafain Churrascaria Dinner Show — backup evening, kept as an option. 7:00 PM: pickup at Sanma (pre-booked hotel transfer — reconfirm the pickup time a day ahead). 7:30 PM: buffet dinner — 200+ hot and cold dishes, salads and desserts, vegetarian-friendly well beyond the grill. ~8:30 PM: the Latin-American dance revue begins — 45+ artists, samba, tango, capoeira and more. ~10:30 PM: show ends, coffee and dessert. ~11:00 PM: transfer back, at Sanma by ~11 PM. Around USD 115–165 per person (2026 prices; recheck for 2027); book in advance with hotel transfers and flag the vegetarian requirement when booking — drinks are typically extra, check at booking. Av. das Cataratas 1749, ~15–20 min from Sanma. If you take this option, it replaces the entire Yup Star + Marco evening — one or the other.
Sunday, Feb 14 — Checkout & Fly Home
Sanma checkout · Pool/spa · IGU → GRU → JFK
8:30 AM
Breakfast, no rush. Last morning in Foz.
9:30–11:00 AM
Final pool/spa morning. One last swim.
11:00 AM
Checkout. Bags stored with the concierge — the room goes, the hotel doesn't (yet).
12:00–1:00 PM
Lunch at the hotel.
Afternoon
Relax — pool, gardens, lobby. Nothing scheduled.
5:30 PM
Taxi to IGU (~10 min; the airport is ~2.6 km from Sanma). Arrive ~6:00 PM — a comfortable 2-hr buffer for the domestic flight.
7:55 PM
Depart IGU → São Paulo (GRU), land 9:45 PM. Connect: depart GRU 11:15 PM → land JFK 7:05 AM, Mon Feb 15. (1.5-hr GRU layover is tight but it's a single booking.)
Base: R. Santa Clara, 405, Copacabana — all timings depart from here. All Uber times include a Carnival-week buffer (add 10–15 min over normal conditions). Weather-sensitive attractions (Cristo, Sugarloaf, Arpoador sunset) are marked ☁️ — see the Weather Strategy block at the bottom of this panel.
Friday, February 5 — Depart New York (JFK)
Overnight flight via Buenos Aires · The trip begins
~7:00 PM
Check in — JFK
Arrive 3 hrs before the 10:00 PM departure. Check bags through to Rio if the booking allows; keep passports handy for Argentine and Brazilian entry.
10:00 PM
Depart JFK → Buenos Aires (EZE)
Overnight flight (~10.5 hrs). Sleep as much as you can — Feb 6 starts the moment you land.
Night
Overnight — en route to EZE
Land Buenos Aires 10:45 AM Saturday, connect 12:45 PM → Rio 3:40 PM. Anyone following the São Paulo pre-Carnival leg (see the São Paulo tab) joins the Rio itinerary here on Feb 6.
Saturday, February 6 — Arrival Day
Settle in · Light orientation · Arpoador sunset
~5:00 PM — On Arrival
Check in · Airbnb at R. Santa Clara, 405
Land 3:40 PM, out of GIG by ~4:15–4:30, 45–60 min transfer — you walk in around 5:00–5:30 PM. Drop luggage. Orient to the apartment. Fill water. Change out of travel clothes. Connect to the wifi and message home. Give this 30 minutes, no more — sunset waits for no one. Do not plan any major sightseeing beyond tonight's plan.
5:30–6:00 PM (Must-Do)
Copacabana Beachfront Walk — Promenade to Arpoador
Walk from R. Santa Clara directly to the beachfront (1 min), turn right onto the famous black-and-white mosaic promenade heading toward Arpoador (~1.4 km, ~15 min at an easy pace). Stop at a padaria on the way for pão de queijo + café — your first real Rio moment. The promenade at golden hour is the perfect jet-lag antidote. Completely free. Carry only your phone and a little cash. You will do this walk many times during the week.
~6:15–6:45 PM (Must-Do) ☁️
Arpoador Rock — Sunset
Walk from Airbnb: ~15 min along the beachfront. Head south on the Copa promenade past the Othon Palace, continue to the end of Copacabana beach, cross the pedestrian bridge to Arpoador Rock. The crowd gathers on the flat granite rock at the tip of the headland between Copa and Ipanema. The sun drops around 6:45 PM — when it does, the crowd applauds. This is free, entirely walkable, and a genuine Rio Carnival-week ritual. Arrive 10–15 min before sunset. Clouds cancel the spectacle — if overcast, skip and come back another evening. Return: same walk, 15 min.
7:30–8:30 PM
Dinner — Ipanema or Copacabana
Two honest options: stay in Ipanema — a 10–15 min walk from Arpoador into the Garota de Ipanema area, livelier dinner scene with more vegetarian-friendly kitchens — or walk back toward the Airbnb for something in Copacabana (Cervantes, Av. Prado Júnior 335 — famous Copa sandwich bar, open late — plus padarias, kiosks, and juice bars within 5 min). Keep it light: you have been traveling for roughly 24 hours. Do not go far. Tomorrow (Feb 7) is an early and full day.
~10:00 PM
Return to Airbnb — Early Night
Unpack properly and lay out tomorrow's sightseeing kit tonight. Confirm the São Paulo → Rio arrival timing — it decides whether everyone meets tonight or tomorrow morning. Feb 7 requires a 6:30 AM wake-up for Cristo. Do not stay out late on arrival night. Carnival bloco energy will be building in the streets — experience it briefly as you walk home, but prioritise sleep.
Pace: Relaxed  ·  Away from Airbnb: 2–4h depending on arrival time  ·  Sightseeing: Orientation only  ·  Walking: All walkable — no Uber needed  ·  Feira do Lavradio: NOT applicable — runs on the last Saturday of each month. Feb 6, 2027 is the first Saturday. Next occurrence: Feb 27, 2027.
Sunday, February 7 — Full Sightseeing Day
Cristo Redentor → Mirante Dona Marta → Santa Teresa → Selarón → Lapa → Bloco evening
6:30 AM
Wake Up — Check the Sky
This is the most important decision of the day. Look at the sky over Corcovado from the window or step outside. Open a weather app. If the summit is clear: proceed with Cristo at 8 AM as planned. If heavily clouded or raining: activate the Weather Swap (see block at the bottom of this panel) and start with Santa Teresa/Selarón/Lapa instead. Do not go up Corcovado in cloud — the view will be zero.
6:45 AM
Breakfast — Near Airbnb
Padaria or café within 5 min walk of R. Santa Clara, 405. Pão de queijo + café com leite or açaí bowl. Keep it fast — you need to depart by 7:30 AM. Do not make a sit-down breakfast. This is a grab-and-go morning.
7:30 AM — Depart Airbnb
→ Cosme Velho (Cristo Redentor tram station) · Uber ~25–35 min (Carnival traffic)
Request Uber on an interior street (Rua Barata Ribeiro or Rua Ministro Viveiros de Castro — not Av. Atlântica). Destination: Rua Cosme Velho, 513 — the Trem do Corcovado station. Distance: ~7 km. Normal: 20 min. Carnival Sunday with some road closures: allow 30–35 min. Surge pricing likely — budget R$40–70.
8:05–8:15 AM ☁️
Cristo Redentor (Corcovado) — Tram Boarding
Booking required in advance: Tickets must be purchased online at tremdocorcovado.rio. Do not show up without a timed ticket — first train is 8 AM and sells out early, especially during Carnival week. Print or screenshot your QR code. Arrive at the station 10 min before your timed departure. The tram ride to the summit takes approximately 20 min each way.
8:30–10:30 AM
Cristo Redentor — Summit
Statue of Christ is 30m tall on a 709m peak with 360° panorama of the city, bay, beaches, and surrounding hills. Spend 1.5–2 hours at the summit — do not rush. Walk the full observation terrace. Photograph the bay from behind the statue (Sugarloaf framed in the distance) and from the front (Copa/Ipanema beaches below). On a clear morning, you can see the Maracanã, the Sambadrome, and the full sweep of Guanabara Bay. Take the tram back down when ready.
10:30 AM — Depart Cosme Velho
→ Mirante Dona Marta · Uber ~15 min
Mirante Dona Marta is on the way from Cosme Velho toward Santa Teresa — it is a natural geographic next stop. Destination: Estrada Dona Marta, Botafogo. Distance: ~3 km from Cosme Velho, 10–15 min Uber.
10:45–11:30 AM ☁️
Mirante Dona Marta — Free Viewpoint
Free outdoor viewpoint at 355m with an exceptional framing: Cristo visible above on the right, Guanabara Bay panorama below, and the city's geography laid out clearly. 30–45 min is enough. No ticket, no booking, no tram — just a short walk to the viewing area. This is the viewpoint that frames Cristo from below — a very different perspective from the summit. Street food vendors and small kiosks are sometimes present on Sundays.
11:30 AM — Depart Mirante Dona Marta
→ Santa Teresa · Uber ~10–12 min
Santa Teresa neighborhood is on the hills above Lapa and the city center — approximately 10 min from Mirante Dona Marta by Uber. Destination: Largo do Guimarães (the main square of Santa Teresa) or your preferred entry point.
11:45 AM–1:30 PM
Santa Teresa — Wander and Lunch
Santa Teresa is Rio's bohemian hillside neighborhood — cobblestone streets, street art, artist studios, colonial houses spilling down toward the city. Walk without a fixed plan. The neighborhood rewards wandering: Largo do Guimarães to Largo das Neves is the main pedestrian axis. Lunch here: Aprazível (Rua Aprazível, 62 — researched, open Sunday, terrace with jungle views; main dishes R$70–120) is the best-known restaurant if budget allows. For a simpler option, Bar do Mineiro (Rua Paschoal Carlos Magno, 99 — a classic boteco, open Sunday, simple Brazilian food, cash preferred). Allow 1.5–2 hours for the walk and lunch combined.
1:30 PM — Depart Santa Teresa
→ Escadaria Selarón · Walk ~20–30 min downhill or Uber ~5 min
Walk downhill from Santa Teresa to the Selarón Steps — this is the classic exit from Santa Teresa. Follow Rua Joaquim Murtinho downhill toward Lapa. The walk takes 20–30 min on cobblestones. If tired: 5 min Uber. Destination: Rua Joaquim Silva, Lapa — the top of the steps.
2:00–2:45 PM
Escadaria Selarón (Selarón Steps)
215 steps covered in 2,000+ ceramic tiles collected from 60+ countries over 20 years by Chilean artist Jorge Selarón (who lived on the steps until his death in 2013). The steps descend toward Lapa from Santa Teresa. Allow 30–45 min — photograph from the bottom looking up, from the top looking down, and find the tiles from your own country. Free. Often crowded on Sundays — arrive before 3 PM if possible. The steps themselves are steep — wear grip shoes.
2:45 PM — Walk
→ Arcos da Lapa · 10-min walk from Selarón base
From the base of the Selarón Steps, walk 10 min toward the Lapa Arches (Arcos da Lapa) — the 18th-century Roman-style aqueduct that now carries the Santa Teresa tram. The arches are most photographed from Rua Riachuelo. By day they are quiet and photogenic; Lapa's famous nightlife scene begins much later (after 11 PM). Spend 20–30 min in the Lapa area. Free.
3:15–4:00 PM
Lapa Arches Area — Optional Café Stop
Rest here before heading south. The area has small cafés and juice bars. Hydrate — it is now midday heat. This is a natural pause before the return journey. If energy is low: head back to the Airbnb now (Uber ~15–20 min, ~8 km). If still going strong: continue to Arpoador for sunset (2.5 hours from now).
4:00 PM — Depart Lapa
→ Airbnb · Uber ~15–20 min
Return to R. Santa Clara, 405. Quick shower and change into bloco clothes — light, comfortable, nothing you mind getting sweaty. This rest is short and non-negotiable: the evening is the main event.
4:00–4:30 PM
Airbnb — Quick Rest & Change
Shower, change, drink water, eat a snack. Pack light for the bloco: phone, some cash, water — minimal valuables. Agree on a meeting point with the group in case anyone gets separated.
4:30–7:00 PM (Must-Do)
Bloco Street Party — Carnival Sunday
Simpatia é Quase Amor (Ipanema) — the target. The best Carnival-Sunday bloco: traditionally parades on this day, 100,000+ people, pure joy. ~15–20 min from the Airbnb. The official 2027 bloco schedule (carnavalderua.rio, published ~Dec/Jan) is the final authority — confirm its parade day and meeting point before the trip. Go with the flow: light clothes, water, minimal valuables, and agree on a meeting point with the group in case anyone gets separated. Since it is beachside, you will catch the ~6:45 PM sunset from the sand — no separate Arpoador trip needed. Note: the Sambadrome's Special Group Night 1 happens tonight across town, but our confirmed Sambadrome night is Feb 9 only.
7:30–8:30 PM
Dinner — Near the Bloco or Copacabana
Keep it simple — you have been on your feet all day. Eat near wherever the bloco ended, or walk back toward Copacabana for padarias, kiosks, and juice bars near the Airbnb. Do not stay out past 10 PM. Tomorrow (Feb 8) is another early start for Sargento Pimenta.
~10:00 PM
Return to Airbnb — Early Night
Walk home or short Uber. Unpack the day bag, lay out tomorrow's kit, sleep. Feb 8 starts at 7 AM.
Pace: Full  ·  Away from Airbnb: ~13h (7:30 AM – 8:30 PM, minus short rest)  ·  Sightseeing: Cristo (~2h) + Mirante (~45 min) + Santa Teresa/lunch (~2h) + Selarón (~45 min) + Lapa (~45 min) + bloco (~2.5h)  ·  Walking: Santa Teresa → Selarón (downhill, 20–30 min) and all flat areas — Uber for hill/distance transfers  ·  Booking required: Cristo tram ticket (tremdocorcovado.rio) — book before departure from home
Monday, February 8 — Full Sightseeing Day
Sargento Pimenta bloco → Sugarloaf Mountain → Ipanema/Arpoador
6:30 AM
Wake Up — Breakfast near Airbnb
Quick breakfast from a padaria or café within 5 min of R. Santa Clara. This is an early start for Sargento Pimenta. Keep breakfast fast. Coffee + pão de queijo or a coxinha. You will eat again at the bloco (food vendors are plentiful).
7:00 AM — Depart Airbnb
→ Aterro do Flamengo · Metro recommended · Siqueira Campos → Catete (~10–12 min)
Take the metro, not an Uber. Carnival Monday creates severe road closures around Flamengo. Metro Line 1: walk to Siqueira Campos station (~8 min from Airbnb) → 3–4 stops to Catete (~10 min) → walk ~8–10 min to Aterro do Flamengo park entrance (Av. Infante Dom Henrique). Metro fare: ~R$5–8. Alternative: Uber directly to Aterro (15–20 min, surge pricing R$30–50). Arrive at the park by 7:50 AM.
8:00 AM–1:30 PM
Sargento Pimenta — Bloco at Aterro do Flamengo
Carnival Monday tradition since the 1990s. A full marching band plays The Beatles' entire catalog as carnival marchinhas — "Yesterday" as a samba, "Let It Be" as pagode, etc. Gathers hundreds of thousands in the large open park along the bay waterfront. Recommended stay: 8 AM – 1:30 PM (3.5–5.5 hours — stay as long as energy holds). The park is large; you can position near the band or find space at the edges. Bring water (vendors everywhere). Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting sweaty and crowded. The bay and Sugarloaf are visible from the park — a beautiful backdrop. Note: 2027 schedule unconfirmed — confirm time via carnaval.rio and Riotur app in January 2027.
1:30 PM — Depart Aterro do Flamengo
→ Sugarloaf (Praia Vermelha cable car base) · Taxi/Uber ~5–7 min
The geographic combination of Sargento Pimenta at Aterro and Sugarloaf in Urca is the most natural pairing on the entire week — they are 4 km apart. Take a taxi or Uber from inside the park. Destination: Praça General Tibúrcio (Praia Vermelha) — the base of the Sugarloaf cable car. Distance: ~4 km, 5–7 min. Budget R$20–35 for the taxi.
2:00–5:30 PM ☁️
Sugarloaf Mountain (Pão de Açúcar)
Cable car runs 8 AM – 9 PM daily. Two cable car stages: Stage 1 from Praia Vermelha to Morro da Urca (212m) — this plateau has a restaurant, amphitheater, and panoramic walkway. Stage 2 from Urca to Sugarloaf summit (396m) — the iconic 38m granite dome. Spend time on BOTH levels. The Urca plateau gives the city panorama; the Sugarloaf summit gives the bay panorama (looking back at the city with Cristo above). Afternoon is excellent timing: golden light begins around 4–5 PM, the bay turns copper, and the city glitters below. No advance booking required for the cable car (buy at the ticket booth), though busy in Carnival week — arrive early in the line. Ticket: approximately R$150–170/person (2026 prices — verify).
5:30 PM — Depart Sugarloaf
→ Airbnb · Uber ~20 min
Uber from Praia Vermelha/Urca back to Copacabana. Distance: ~7 km. Normal: 15 min. Carnival Monday traffic: allow 20–25 min. Budget R$30–50 surge.
6:00–7:00 PM
Airbnb — Rest
Quick rest, shower, and change before the evening. Tomorrow is Feb 9 — Camarote Mar. Tonight is a moderate evening, not a late night. Do not overdo it tonight.
6:15 PM (Optional) ☁️
Arpoador Sunset — Optional if energy remains
If still energetic after the bloco + Sugarloaf: walk to Arpoador (15 min). Sunset ~6:36 PM on Feb 8 — aim to be on the rock by 6:15 PM. This is genuinely optional — today was already a full day. Skip if tired. The bloco + Sugarloaf combination is the primary plan.
7:30 PM
Dinner — Copacabana or Ipanema
Keep dinner close to the Airbnb tonight. Tomorrow is Feb 9 (Carnival night) and you need good sleep. Copacabana has plenty of restaurants and kiosks within a 5-min walk. Light-to-moderate dinner. No alcohol excess tonight — tomorrow requires stamina until dawn.
9:00–9:30 PM
Return to Airbnb — Moderate Early Night
Back at the Airbnb (R. Santa Clara, 405) by 9:30 PM. Lights out by 10 PM. Tomorrow: sleep in, no alarm, rest day before Camarote Mar.
Pace: Full  ·  Away from Airbnb: ~12h (7 AM – 7 PM)  ·  Sightseeing: Sargento Pimenta (~5h) + Sugarloaf (~3.5h)  ·  Walking: Metro to Aterro · taxi to Sugarloaf · Uber home  ·  Booking: Sugarloaf buy at ticket booth — no advance booking needed but Carnival week is busy; arrive mid-afternoon (2 PM) to avoid morning rushes
Tuesday, February 9 — Camarote Mar · Carnival Night
Urca · Praia Vermelha · Pista Cláudio Coutinho · rest · prepare · Sambadrome
Day structure: This is Terça-feira Gorda (Carnival Tuesday) — the final and busiest day of street Carnival. The Sambadrome tonight is the main event. The morning is for a genuine Rio experience that is low-effort, close to base, and finished by 1 PM. The afternoon is fully protected for rest and preparation. Orquestra Voadora — the large bloco at Aterro do Flamengo — parades from ~3 PM, which conflicts directly with the required rest window before the Sambadrome. It is not an option for this day. Blocos on Tuesday morning (before noon) are limited among the major names; none make sense ahead of a Sambadrome night. Selected morning: Urca neighborhood + Praia Vermelha + Pista Cláudio Coutinho — 3.7 km from the Airbnb, entirely low-effort, authentically local, and unlike anything else in this itinerary. Backup morning (kept, not replacing): Jardim Botânico + Parque Lage — the two remaining top-10 sights, ~10 min apart, equally low-effort (8:45 AM Uber → 9:15–10:15 AM Parque Lage, free, opens 9 AM → 10:30 AM–12:00 PM Jardim Botânico, opens 8 AM Tue, ~R$75–80/person, book online). Pick the backup to complete all 10 top sights; keep Urca for the beach-trail-local morning. Either way, back by 12:30 PM.
8:00 AM
Wake Up — Breakfast near Airbnb
Quick breakfast from a padaria or café within 5 min of R. Santa Clara. Pão de queijo, fruit, coffee or açaí. Keep it light — you will eat again mid-morning at the Mureta da Urca. Depart by 8:45 AM.
8:45 AM — Depart Airbnb
→ Praia Vermelha · Uber ~10–15 min · ~3.7 km
Request Uber from Rua Barata Ribeiro (one block inland — avoid Av. Atlântica on Carnival Tuesday morning). Destination: Praça General Tibúrcio — the plaza directly in front of Praia Vermelha beach. Distance: 3.7 km. Normal: 10 min. Carnival Tuesday with morning road closures: allow 15 min. Budget R$20–30. Do not be deterred by the Carnival noise on the way — Urca itself is one of the quietest places in Rio on any day, including Carnival.
9:00–9:15 AM
Praia Vermelha — Arrive and Orientate
Praia Vermelha is a small (245 m), sheltered cove at the base of Morro da Urca — completely calm water, surrounded by Atlantic Forest on the hillside, with the first cable car stage visible above you. This is one of Rio's most striking contrasts: an intimate, quiet beach with Sugarloaf directly overhead. Spend 10–15 minutes on the beach before starting the trail. There are food kiosks at the plaza — buy a cold water or coconut water here before walking.
9:15–10:00 AM
Pista Cláudio Coutinho — Atlantic Forest Trail
Access: from the Praia Vermelha beach, follow the signed path to the right of the beach toward Morro da Urca. The Pista Cláudio Coutinho is a 1.25 km paved flat trail (no elevation — it runs level along the base of the hill) through dense Atlantic Forest. Open 6 AM – 6 PM daily. Free. The trail is in the shade the entire way. What you will see: bromeliads and orchids on the trees, howler monkeys (common in this section), marmosets, ocean views through the canopy at several points, and the granite face of Morro da Urca rising above you. The trail ends at a gate on the Urca neighborhood side. Walk as far as you want and return the same way — you do not need to complete the full length. 30–45 min of walking is ideal. Flat, paved, low effort.
10:00–10:30 AM
Praia Vermelha — Beach Time
Return from the trail to Praia Vermelha beach. Sit on the sand for 20–30 min. The beach faces Guanabara Bay — the water is sheltered and calm, very different from Copa or Ipanema. You are looking directly at Niterói across the bay. Sugarloaf is directly above to your right. This is a completely different Rio beach experience from the Atlantic-facing beaches you have visited elsewhere this week.
10:30 AM — Walk (~10 min)
→ Mureta da Urca · Rua Cândido Gaffrée · 10-min flat walk through Urca
Walk from Praia Vermelha around the base of the hill and into the Urca neighborhood. The walk takes about 10 min on flat residential streets. Urca is genuinely village-like: quiet streets, colonial houses, residents sitting outside, essentially no tourists. You will not feel like you are in a major city. The contrast with the rest of Carnival week is the point.
10:40–11:30 AM
Mureta da Urca — Locals' Waterfront Scene
Mureta da Urca is a low concrete wall along the waterfront of Urca facing Guanabara Bay — a genuine neighborhood institution. Locals, retirees, and regulars come here to sit on the wall with cold chopp (draft beer poured from mobile carts) and eat pastel (fried pastry). The view from the wall: Niterói and the bay directly ahead, the Rio-Niterói bridge visible in the distance, and Sugarloaf rising above to your left. This is a scene that does not exist in tourist brochures. For vegetarians: pastel de queijo (cheese-filled fried pastry) is the go-to — available from all the food carts along the Mureta. Água de coco is always available. Pão de queijo may also be sold. Spend 45–50 min here. Budget R$20–40 for drinks and snacks.
11:30 AM — Depart Mureta da Urca
→ Airbnb · Uber ~15 min · ~4 km
Request Uber from Rua Cândido Gaffrée in Urca. Distance: ~4 km to R. Santa Clara, 405. Allow 15 min with Carnival Tuesday traffic. Budget R$20–35. Back at the Airbnb by noon–12:30 PM.
12:30–1:30 PM
Lunch — Near Airbnb (substantial, vegetarian-friendly)
Eat a proper lunch now, close to the Airbnb. Options within 5–10 min: Zona Sul supermarket (Rua Barata Ribeiro, 489 — prepared food counter, rice and beans, salads, açaí, fruit); or a sit-down café/restaurant in Copa. This is an important meal — eat well, as your next proper meal will be at ~5:30 PM before leaving for the Sambadrome. Rehydrate seriously during lunch. Do not rush.
1:30–3:30 PM
Airbnb — Rest Block · Mandatory
Rest is not optional today. You attended a full sightseeing day yesterday (Feb 8) and are heading to a 9-hour Sambadrome event tonight that runs until 5–6 AM. Lie down. Nap if possible. Drink water consistently. Do not watch anything stressful. Do not go out. Do not drink alcohol. This 2-hour rest window is the single most important preparation for the Camarote Mar experience.
3:30–5:00 PM
Preparation — Shower · Dress · Charge · Pack
Shower, dress, and pack your essentials for the Sambadrome. What to bring: comfortable shoes you can stand in for 7–8 hours; a small bag or backpack (check what is permitted by the Camarote Mar's bag policy in your booking docs); small cash R$100–200 for incidentals (confirm inclusions in the camarote — food and drink are typically included but some items may not be); your booking QR code (printed or screenshot on your phone); phone charged to 100%; a light jacket or layer (camarote interiors can be air-conditioned); a portable charger if you have one. Do not bring valuables you cannot keep on your body. Leave large bags at the Airbnb.
5:30 PM
Dinner — Near Airbnb (proper meal before leaving)
Eat a real meal before leaving. Even with food available at Camarote Mar, you will not properly eat for several hours after leaving. Keep it filling but not heavy: rice + beans + salad from a nearby restaurant, or a padaria with hot food. Zona Sul supermarket prepared foods are practical if you do not want to go to a restaurant. Nothing greasy — something digestible. No alcohol at this meal.
Confirm from Booking Documentation
Meeting Time at Othon Palace — Check Your Docs Before This Day
The exact meeting/departure time at Othon Palace must be confirmed from your Camarote Mar booking documentation. Camarote Mar typically assembles groups 1–2 hours before the parade start (~9 PM), suggesting a meeting time in the 7–8 PM range, but this varies by year and package. Check your confirmation email or booking PDF. Set a phone alarm 30 min before the confirmed meeting time. Do not rely on this guide for the exact time.
Confirmed Meeting Time minus 10 min
Walk to Othon Palace · Av. Atlântica, 3264 · 5-min walk from Airbnb
Walk, do not Uber. R. Santa Clara, 405 → Av. Atlântica → left along the beachfront ~300m → Othon Palace Copacabana. A 3–5 minute walk. No vehicle needed. Arrive at least 10 min before the confirmed meeting time. Camarote Mar provides group transport from this meeting point to Sector 6 of the Sambadrome — do not attempt to travel to the Sambadrome independently by Uber on a Special Group parade night.
~9:00–9:30 PM
Sambadrome — Parades Begin · Special Group Night 3
The final and most prestigious parade night — the last 4 elite samba schools compete and cumulative energy peaks. Camarote Mar is in Sector 6, a covered premium viewing area with food and drink service. Each school takes approximately 1.5–2 hours. Total duration: approximately 7–8 hours, running until ~5–6 AM on Feb 10.
~3:30–5:00 AM (Feb 10)
Return from Sambadrome
Camarote Mar return transport — INCLUDED in your ticket: after the final parade, return transfers run from the Sambadrome pickup area back to the Othon Palace meeting point — then the 5-min walk back to the Airbnb at R. Santa Clara, 405. (Night 3 has 4 schools, so parades wrap ~3 AM; expect to be in bed by ~5 AM.) Fallback if ever needed: Metro Line 2 from Praça Onze (runs 24h on all three parade nights) → transfer at Central do Brasil → Line 1 → Siqueira Campos → walk 8 min. Every night ends at the Airbnb — no exceptions. Late-night safety: walk from Othon Palace/Siqueira Campos as a group, stick to well-lit main streets (Av. Atlântica / Rua Barata Ribeiro), and carry minimal valuables to the Sambadrome — phone, ticket, some cash, nothing more.
Pace: Light morning (3–4h) · protected afternoon · intense night  ·  Morning back at Airbnb: by 12:30 PM  ·  Rest block begins: 1:30 PM  ·  Hard constraint: Camarote Mar, Sector 6, Sambadrome — this overrides everything  ·  Return to Airbnb: ~4–5 AM, February 10
☁️ Weather backup (if heavy rain at 8 AM): Skip Urca. Walk along the Copa beachfront to Forte de Copacabana (2.5 km, 30 min along the beach, or 10-min Uber). The fort opens at 10 AM Tuesday–Sunday. Entry is free on Tuesdays (follow their Instagram). The military history museum + Confeitaria Colombo cafe branch inside the fort takes 2–2.5 hours. Views from the ramparts look back up the full length of Copacabana Beach and out to sea. Return to Airbnb by noon. The fort is sheltered and partially covered — rain does not cancel it. Adjust departure to 9:30 AM to align with opening.
Wednesday, February 10 — Recovery + Fly to Iguazu
Late wake · Brunch near Airbnb · Pack · Checkout · GIG → IGU · Hotel Night 1
5:00–6:00 AM
Return from Sambadrome / Arrive Airbnb
You are returning from the Sambadrome now. Go straight to bed. No alarm set. Pack before leaving for the Sambadrome if you can — checkout is ~1:00 PM today, so bags should be nearly ready at the door.
12:00 PM
Wake Up — Soft Alarm at Noon
A soft noon alarm — the 4:25 PM flight means checkout is ~1:00 PM, so sleeping until 2 PM is not an option today. Recovery sleep still matters: you got the core hours after the 5–6 AM Carnival return.
12:00–12:45 PM
Brunch — At or Near Airbnb Only
Açaí bowl, pão de queijo, fruit, coffee. Stay within 5 min of the Airbnb — a padaria on the block or the Zona Sul supermarket (Rua Barata Ribeiro, 489). Rehydrate seriously. You will miss the Apuração (~3 PM) — accept it.
12:45–1:15 PM
Final Pack + Checkout — R. Santa Clara, 405
Pack everything for Iguazu (4 nights: Feb 10–13). Charge all devices, locate passports (needed for the Argentine border crossing on Feb 12). Final sweep, lock up, return keys. Standard checkout applies — the late-checkout plan died with the old evening-flight assumption.
1:30 PM
→ GIG Terminal 2 — Uber ~45–55 min
Depart the Airbnb by 1:30 PM. Arrive GIG ~2:30 PM — a comfortable buffer for the 4:25 PM domestic departure.
4:25 PM
GOL G3 1866 — GIG → IGU
Direct 2h15m, Boeing 737-800, departing Terminal 2. Land IGU 6:40 PM.
6:40–7:30 PM
Arrive IGU → Sanma Hotel by Nobile
Pre-booked private transfer (~25 min). Check in ~7:15 PM. Tonight's job: buy Feb 11 tickets online — Brazilian park (~R$134/person) at tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br and Macuco Safari (~R$386/person) at macucosafari.com.br. Light dinner, sleep.
Thursday, February 11 — Full Day: Brazilian Side
Parque Nacional do Iguaçu · Macuco Safari · Trilha das Cataratas · Early Night
📋

Park entry — tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br, ~R$134/adult (foreigner rate). Date-specific; enter any time during opening hours. Macuco Safari — macucosafari.com.br, ~R$386/person (2026 figure — recheck for 2027). No time slot: boats depart every ~15–20 min from 9:00 AM. Park admission is not included in the Macuco price — you need both tickets. Parque das Aves (optional) — ~R$80, buy at the door. Total ≈ R$600. Buying online the night before means zero ticket lines in the morning.

📋

Swimsuit or quick-dry clothes + sandals (boat), full change of dry clothes, plastic bag for wet gear, waterproof phone pouch, ≥1.5 L water, trail snacks, DEET, sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, small towel, R$300–500 cash + Visa. Leave passport in the hotel safe — no border crossing today.

7:00 AM
Wake up at Sanma
Full park day — the biggest single day of the Iguazu portion. No border crossing: both hotel and park are in Brazil, so the passport stays in the hotel safe. The park opens at 9:00 AM on weekdays (last entry 4:00 PM); arriving early beats the midday crowds and the worst of the February heat.
7:30 AM
Breakfast at Sanma (included)
Brazilian hotel breakfasts are a vegetarian's dream — tropical fruits, breads, cheeses, eggs, tapioca, cakes. Eat a proper meal: you will walk several kilometres in February humidity and get soaked by mid-morning. Drink plenty of water, apply sunscreen now, and fill your water bottles — there is nothing to drink between the trailhead and lunch.
8:20 AM
Leave Sanma on foot
The park entrance is an 8-minute walk along Rodovia das Cataratas — flat, straightforward, no Uber needed. Daypack check: swimsuit/quick-dry clothes on or packed, full change of clothes, plastic bag for wet gear, waterproof phone pouch, DEET, hat, water, snacks, cash + card.
8:30 AM
At the visitor-center turnstiles
The Centro de Visitantes: turnstiles, shops, restrooms, café. Show your online QR and walk straight through — no ticket line. The park opens at 9:00 AM, so you are near the front of the line on a peak-season February morning. Use the restrooms here; the next facilities are at the Macuco dock.
9:00 AM
First park shuttle bus to Stop 1
Private cars cannot enter the park — everyone rides the included buses, every ~10–15 min, three hop-on/hop-off stops, no separate fare or reservation. Ride to Stop 1: the Macuco Safari dock.
9:15–11:15 AM
Macuco Safari (~2 hrs, three stages)
① 3 km open-cart jungle ride through Atlantic rainforest with a bilingual guide. ② 600 m suspended forest walkway to the base deck — lockers, restrooms, snack bar; stash dry clothes here. ③ Twin-engine boats up the river through rapids, driven directly under the cascades. Life jackets provided; the operator runs under a federal concession with Inmetro/ABNT safety certification. You will be completely soaked — that is the point.

Tickets — two required, bought separately: ① Park admission ~R$134/adult (foreigner rate) at tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br. ② Macuco Safari ticket ~R$386/person at macucosafari.com.br (official site). The Macuco price does not include park entry. Book both online on Feb 10 night — do not buy at the dock in February. Peak-season days sell out, and pre-booked visitors get priority boarding; buying at the dock is possible but risks sellout plus a second queue. With both QRs on your phone the morning is frictionless: turnstiles (no line) → shuttle → Stop 1 → straight into the next departing group. Even pre-booked, expect a short boarding wait — the 9:00 AM first departures keep it minimal, while later in the day waits can stretch past an hour. (A private no-queue option exists at R$597/person with towels, raincoats, drinks and lunch box — but it needs 4+ paying adults and a prior appointment.)
11:15–11:30 AM
Change into dry clothes
at the dock deck's restrooms and lockers. Wet gear goes into the zip bag — you are dry for the rest of the day. Snack bar and souvenir shop at the deck while you regroup.
11:30 AM
Shuttle to Stop 2: Trilha das Cataratas trailhead
Short ride. Use the restrooms here — the trail is effectively one-way with no facilities until the end at Porto Canoas.
11:45 AM–1:15 PM
Trilha das Cataratas (1.2 km, ~90 min)
Paved, mostly flat trail with frontal viewpoints across the gorge — the only place all ~275 falls appear in one panorama. Coatis roam the trail (don't feed them). Finale: the metal walkway jutting over the river directly in front of the Devil's Throat — deafening, mist-soaked, rainbows — then the panoramic glass elevator to the top deck.
1:15–2:15 PM
Lunch at Porto Canoas
(trail's end, open 12:00–4:00 PM). Buffet with river views, confirmed vegetarian-friendly with plenty of vegan options. Caution: black beans are often cooked with pork and farofa may contain bacon — ask staff before serving. Drinks and desserts extra. Rest your legs — you have earned it.
2:15–2:45 PM
Upper deck & Espaço Naipi
Final panoramic photos with the full sweep of the falls from above, plus a gift shop for souvenirs. The classic postcard angle — the wide shot of the entire system you cannot get anywhere else.
3:00–4:15 PM
Optional: Parque das Aves
Bird park beside the park entrance (~4 min walk from Sanma): 150+ species — toucans, macaws, flamingos — in walk-through aviaries. ~R$80, ~1.5 hrs, no booking, vegetarian-friendly café. Skip guilt-free if tired. Note: take the park shuttle back to the visitor center first, then walk to the bird park entrance.
4:30 PM
Last return shuttle from Stop 3 — do not miss it
The park day ends at 5:00 PM; this bus carries you back to the visitor center. Be at the stop with time to spare. (If you did Parque das Aves, you are already at the entrance.)
5:00–5:15 PM
Walk back to Sanma
(8 min). Shower, rest 60–90 min. Confirm tomorrow's Argentine-side transfer at the front desk if you have not already.
7:00 PM
Dinner — Near Sanma
Light dinner near the hotel — the Rafain Show moved to Feb 13 (backup option). Keep tonight simple: the Argentine side starts at 6:00 AM tomorrow.
8:30 PM
Pack for Argentina — Sleep
Pack tomorrow's daypack tonight: same kit minus the swimsuit, broken-in walking shoes, and passport in the bag — Friday means a border crossing, with 45–90 min of formalities before you reach the Argentine park. Lights out early.
✅

☐ Park ticket online (tickets.cataratasdoiguacu.com.br), QR downloaded offline · ☐ Macuco Safari ticket (macucosafari.com.br) · ☐ Confirm Feb 12 Argentine transfer at Sanma's front desk · ☐ Pack daypack per the list above · ☐ Notify bank of Brazil/Argentina travel dates.

💰

Money. International Visa works everywhere that matters (park, Macuco, restaurants, Uber). Carry R$300–500 cash for kiosks, small vendors, taxis. Always pay in reais (BRL), never USD, at card terminals.

Friday, February 12 — Full Day: Argentine Side
Border crossing · Parque Nacional Iguazú · Garganta del Diablo · Lower + Upper Circuits
⚠️ Check before you go (Jan 2027): as of September 2026, the Devil's Throat walkway on the Argentine side is temporarily closed (sections removed as a precaution against high river levels). Verify it has reopened before Feb 12 — if still closed, reallocate the morning to the Lower and Upper circuits.
6:00 AM
Wake Up — Sanma Hotel, Foz do Iguaçu
This schedule puts you at the Argentine park around 8:30 AM — on one of the first Ecological Trains to Devil's Throat, still well ahead of the tour-bus crowds. The border crossing adds ~80–95 min of travel before you reach the park. Lay out the daypack the night before: passport in an easily reachable pocket, park ticket QR screenshotted offline, water, snacks, sunscreen, DEET, poncho, waterproof phone pouch. Hydrate as soon as you wake.
6:30–7:00 AM
Breakfast — Restaurante Amaru, Sanma Hotel (included)
A full, unhurried 30 minutes — the buffet opens at 6:30 AM sharp (served daily 6:30–10:30 AM, included in your rate — verified). Fresh fruit, breads, and the made-to-order station (tapioca, eggs — vegetarian-friendly). You will not sit down for lunch until ~11:15, and the morning is immigration lines plus the 1.1 km Devil's Throat catwalk, so eat properly. Fill your water bottles here. Apply sunscreen and DEET before leaving; the Argentine trails are humid rainforest. Wear broken-in walking shoes — 6–8 km of walking today, and the Lower Circuit has steep wet stairs.
7:00 AM — Depart Hotel
→ Ponte Tancredo Neves (Brazil–Argentina border) · ~15 min by pre-arranged taxi/remise
Meet your driver in the lobby — arranged at Sanma's front desk the night before, fixed round-trip price agreed in advance, driver waits through both immigration posts and the ~7-hour park visit. Do NOT rely on Uber: Uber does not quote cross-border trips and drivers routinely refuse them. Confirm the price and the waiting/pickup arrangement one more time before getting in. At 7:00 AM the roads are still quiet — the tour buses head out later.
~7:15 AM — Border Crossing — Brazil Exit
Polícia Federal — Brazilian immigration (exit stamp)
The taxi stops at the Brazilian immigration post. Exit the vehicle with your passport — the driver waits with the car; he cannot clear immigration for you. Join the exit queue, present your passport and complete Brazilian exit formalities — exact procedures depend on your nationality and 2027 rules, so confirm before travel. At this hour it is usually 10–15 minutes, before any tour-bus traffic. (Some day-trippers skip this post since they return the same evening — do not. You need a clean re-entry stamp when you fly out of IGU on Feb 14.)
~7:30 AM — The Bridge
Ponte Tancredo Neves — cross the Iguaçu River into Argentina
About five minutes of driving; the actual country line is mid-bridge over the Iguaçu River. Have your passport ready. Argentine entry requirements vary by nationality and may include pre-registration — confirm the 2027 rules for your passports before travel, and ask your driver in transit what the current procedure is. No stop on the bridge itself; the Argentine post is on the far side.
~7:40 AM — Border Crossing — Argentina Entry
Dirección Nacional de Migraciones — Argentine immigration (entry stamp)
Second stop: get out with your passport and completed entry form. Queue, present documents and answer the standard questions (where are you staying? how long?). Whether you receive a stamp or slip depends on nationality and current procedures — keep whatever they give you. Before 8:00 AM you are still ahead of the tour-bus wave: typically 15–25 minutes at this hour, versus 45+ later in the morning. Your driver waits; agree beforehand where he will park. Both crossings together at this hour: usually under an hour.
~8:05–8:25 AM
→ Parque Nacional Iguazú · ~20 min by taxi/remise
Drive from the Argentine border post past Puerto Iguazú town to the park entrance on RN 101 (~20 min). Your round trip is already agreed and paid in reais — no new negotiation. The driver waits at the park while you visit (typically 6–7 hours) — agree the exact pickup meeting point and time now. Use the restrooms at the visitor center before entering.
8:25–8:40 AM
Enter Parque Nacional Iguazú (Argentine entrance)
Through the turnstiles with your pre-bought QR from ventaweb.apn.gob.ar (official National Parks portal, ~ARS 35,000–45,000 per foreign adult — 2026 figure, recheck for 2027; about USD 26–35). Tickets are not reliably sold at the gate, so online in advance is the safe play in February. The ticket includes the Ecological Train and all three circuits. Collect a park map at the entrance. Head straight for Estación Central — the Ecological Train departure point. You will likely catch the second train to Garganta station (~8:50 AM).
~8:50 AM
→ Eco-Train to Garganta Station (~20 min)
Board the open-air Ecological Train at Estación Central, destination Garganta Station. The ~20 min ride cuts through dense Atlantic Forest canopy — keep the camera ready for toucans, monkeys, and coatis along the track. Trains run continuously through the day and are included in your ticket. This is the only motorized transport inside the park; everything else is on foot. Devil's Throat first is the entire strategy: smallest crowds, best light, shortest train queues.
~9:10 AM
Garganta Station → 1.1 km catwalk to the viewpoint
From the station, a flat elevated metal catwalk crosses the upper Iguaçu River — the river fans into dozens of channels across the floodplain before dropping simultaneously into the gorge. You hear the falls long before you see them. The walkway is 100% accessible and flat; allow ~25 minutes each way at a photo-stop pace. (If the walkway is still closed from the 2026 high-water works, reallocate this block: extend the Lower Circuit and add the Argentine Macuco jungle trail.)
9:20–10:20 AM
Garganta del Diablo — Devil's Throat Platform
The centerpiece of Iguazu — both sides, any season, any visitor. The platform sits directly above the horseshoe-shaped chasm — note the catwalk has closed for repairs in past years, so recheck Devil's Throat access status shortly before travel (82 m deep, 150 m wide) where half the river's flow plunges at once. In February, at peak water volume, the falls dissolve into white thunder and the roar is physical. The spray is total — poncho on, phone in the waterproof pouch. You are still well ahead of the midday crowds. Allow up to 45 minutes; it never gets old. Then walk the catwalk back to Garganta Station.
10:35–11:05 AM
→ Eco-Train back to Estación Cataratas (~15 min)
Board the train back to the middle station, Estación Cataratas. Restrooms, water refill, regroup. You are now switching from the panoramic morning to the immersive afternoon.
11:15 AM–12:15 PM
Lunch — Main Restaurant Complex near Estación Cataratas
Lunch at the park's main restaurant complex — still ahead of the worst of the noon rush. Full restaurants and snack bars; vegetarian options are usually available — empanadas de verdura (vegetable empanadas), pasta, salads — but ask about meat stock (¿Tiene caldo de carne?) the way you would ask about pork in Brazil. Drinks and desserts extra. Rest your legs properly: the afternoon is ~3.5 km of walking with stairs. Refill water bottles.
12:30–2:30 PM
Circuito Inferior (Lower Circuit) — 1.7 km, ~2 hrs
The most immersive circuit in the park: the trail descends into the gorge and runs along the base of multiple falls at water level — you feel the falls rather than just seeing them, including the viewpoint at the boat dock facing the cascades head-on. This is the wettest and most physically demanding section: steep descents and ascents, slippery surfaces, sturdy shoes essential (sandals are not suitable). Coatis, butterflies, and rainbows in the spray everywhere. Do not feed the coatis.
2:45–4:00 PM
Circuito Superior (Upper Circuit) — 1.4–1.9 km, ~1–1.5 hrs
The panoramic circuit: mostly flat elevated walkways along the top of the falls, looking down the drop line of the major cascades, with the jungle canopy and the canyon spreading below — the wide-angle complement to the morning's close-ups. Calmer, drier, and the gentlest walking of the three circuits. Done by ~4:00 PM, before the falls areas begin closing.
4:00–4:30 PM
Exit Argentine Park — meet driver
Walk out to the park entrance and meet your driver at the agreed spot. Restrooms, water, final souvenir check at the park shops. Confirm the return route — same two posts in reverse.
4:30–5:30 PM
Border Crossing — Argentina Exit + Brazil Entry
Reverse the morning: Argentine exit formalities (usually quick), bridge, Brazilian entry formalities. Same drill — you get out with your passport at each post, the driver waits. Late-afternoon crossings are typically faster than morning ones, but Friday traffic can bunch up; budget up to an hour. The Brazilian re-entry stamp is the one that matters for your Feb 14 flight out of IGU — make sure you get it.
5:45–6:00 PM
→ Sanma Hotel · ~15–20 min from border
Back at the hotel by ~6:00 PM. Shower and change. You have been walking 6+ hours in heat and humidity across two countries — take a proper rest before dinner. The hardest day of the Iguazu portion is behind you.
7:00 PM
Dinner — Hotel or Nearby, Foz do Iguaçu
The hotel restaurant is the most practical option after a full day. Alternatively, Foz has reasonable options near the park corridor — agree any taxi price before getting in. Vegetarian-friendly choices are easy to find; eat well, you have earned it. Tomorrow (Feb 13) is your free day: no alarm, no border, no schedule.
9:30 PM
Hotel — Rest
Lights out. Optional: sketch your Feb 13 free-day plan — Itaipu Dam (panoramic or special tour, book via the hotel), Parque das Aves (if skipped on Feb 11), Puerto Iguazú town across the border, or a genuine rest day by the pool. No tickets to buy tonight, no early alarm tomorrow.
Saturday, February 13 — Free Day in Foz
No alarm · Parque das Aves · Itaipu Dam · Yup Star + Triple Frontier evening · Rafain (backup)
Morning — no alarm
Sleep In — Sanma Hotel
Two huge falls days are behind you. Wake when you wake; relaxed breakfast at the hotel (served 6:30–10:30 AM). Today moves at your pace.
10:00 AM–12:30 PM
Parque das Aves — Bird Park
A 4-minute walk from Sanma (~R$110 at the door, 2026 prices; recheck for 2027). Walk-through aviaries with toucans, macaws, and parrots — 2 to 3 hours, no booking needed. The natural pairing with the Brazilian falls day, kept deliberately for the free day so Feb 11 stays unhurried.
12:30–1:30 PM
Lunch — At or Near the Hotel
Keep it simple and vegetarian-friendly; rest your feet.
2:00–5:00 PM
Itaipu Dam — Panoramic Tour
One of the world's largest hydroelectric dams, ~20 min from Foz. Book the panoramic tour via the hotel front desk (hotel-pickup tours ~USD 35–40, 2026 prices); the special behind-the-scenes tour (~R$182) goes inside the dam if you want the deeper version. About 3 hours including transfers.
5:30–6:15 PM
Yup Star — Ferris Wheel at Sunset
88m high with air-conditioned cabins, ~20-min ride, 360° views over the triple-border region where the Iguaçu and Paraná rivers meet (~R$60–79, open daily 12:30–8:30 PM). The standout moment of the day — sunset with Brazil, Argentina, and Paraguay spread out below. Right by the Marco complex, so the two pair naturally.
6:30–8:30 PM
Marco das Três Fronteiras — Cultural Show + Dinner
Where Brazil, Argentina, and Paraguay meet at the river confluence. Entry ~R$55–60; cultural show ~6:30 PM (~2 hrs); dinner at the Cabeza de Vaca restaurant inside the complex. Back at Sanma ~9 PM. Skip without guilt if you'd rather rest — the pool and spa are the fallback, and the Guarani Village cultural visit is the alternative if you'd rather do that than the dam.
7:00–11:00 PM (backup option)
Rafain Churrascaria — Dinner Show (kept as backup)
Foz's classic dinner show, kept as your backup evening. 7:00 PM: pickup at Sanma — pre-booked hotel transfer (reconfirm the pickup time a day ahead). 7:30 PM: buffet dinner — 200+ hot and cold dishes, salads, desserts; vegetarian-friendly well beyond the grill. ~8:30 PM: the Latin-American dance revue begins — 45+ artists, samba, tango, capoeira and more. ~10:30 PM: show ends, coffee and dessert. ~11:00 PM: transfer back to Sanma. Around USD 115–165 per person (2026 prices; recheck for 2027); book in advance with hotel transfers and flag the vegetarian requirement when booking — drinks are typically extra, check at booking. Av. das Cataratas 1749, ~15–20 min from Sanma. Taking this replaces the entire Yup Star + Marco evening — it's one or the other.

Sanma checkout · Pool/spa · IGU → GRU → JFK

No rush. Last morning in Foz — pack what's left after breakfast.

One last swim. Confirm checkout time and baggage storage with the front desk.

The room goes, the hotel doesn't (yet). Keep a day bag with swim gear and a change of clothes.
12:00–1:00 PM

Nothing scheduled. Rest before the overnight journey.

~10 min; the airport is ~2.6 km from Sanma. Arrive ~6:00 PM — a comfortable 2-hour buffer for the domestic flight. Keep passports accessible.

Land GRU 9:45 PM. Connect: depart GRU 11:15 PM → land JFK 7:05 AM, Monday Feb 15. The 1.5-hour GRU layover is tight but it's a single booking — the airline handles the connection.

Weather Strategy — Simple Swap Rules

Primary Rule: Cristo and Sugarloaf get the two clearest mornings

These are the two weather-sensitive panoramic viewpoints. Cristo goes on the clearest of Feb 7 or Feb 8. Sugarloaf goes on the other. Do not visit either in cloud — the view is the point.

If Feb 7 morning is clear → Cristo on Feb 7 (as planned)

Full Cluster A as written: Cristo → Mirante Dona Marta → Santa Teresa → Selarón → Lapa → Arpoador.

If Feb 7 morning is cloudy → Swap

Start Feb 7 with Santa Teresa → Selarón → Lapa (weather-independent). Reserve Cristo for Feb 8 morning. Move Sargento Pimenta to whenever Cristo clears, or attend the bloco and skip Cristo until the Tijuca tab's Cristo fallback.

Arpoador sunset — any clear evening works

Available on any clear evening during Feb 6–10. If clouds cancel it on one evening, simply walk over on the next clear one.

Feb 10 (Recovery + Departure) — rain is irrelevant

Feb 10 has no outdoor activity — recovery, packing, and an evening airport run. Rain does not affect this day. Stay near the Airbnb. Order delivery if needed. Leave for GIG by 5 PM regardless.

Iguazu (Feb 11–13) — rain does NOT cancel Iguazu

February is the wettest and most spectacular month at Iguazu Falls — peak water flow means the falls are at their most powerful. Rain makes trails slippery (particularly Argentine Lower Circuit) but does not close the parks. Bring a rain poncho for every Iguazu day — especially Garganta del Diablo where spray is total regardless of weather. The falls are the destination; rain is part of the experience.

Iguazu weather backup — if Argentine Lower Circuit closes (rare)

In extreme peak-water years, sections of the Argentine Lower Circuit may temporarily close due to flooding. REQUIRES VERIFICATION at travel time. If closed: focus on Garganta del Diablo + Upper Circuit (Argentine side) or add extra time on the Brazilian Trilha das Cataratas. The Macuco Safari boat operates independently of trail closures.

Sambadrome Nights Overview

Three Special Group nights, Feb 7–9. We have a confirmed booking for Feb 9 only. Feb 7 and 8 are separate events — tickets for those nights would need to be purchased separately if desired.

Sunday, Feb 7 — Night 1

First 4 elite samba schools. Starts ~9pm, ends ~5–6am. We do not have a ticket for this night. Attending blocos during the day is an alternative way to experience Carnival energy.

Monday, Feb 8 — Night 2

Next 4 schools. Peak energy. We do not have a ticket for this night. The remaining 4 schools from Night 2 are considered among the competition's most hotly contested.

Tuesday, Feb 9 — Night 3 ✓ OUR NIGHT

Final 4 schools. Most prestigious night — traditional winner is often announced in the days following, but the final night's energy is the highest of the three. Our confirmed Camarote Mar booking.

Saturday, Feb 13 — Champions' Parade

Top schools parade again after the champion is announced. More festive, less intense. Falls within a future trip — worth attending if extending. Separate tickets required.

Rio sightseeing blocks: Feb 6 (arrival/orientation), Feb 7 (Cristo + Lapa), Feb 8 (Sugarloaf), Feb 9 (Urca half-day + Sambadrome). Feb 10 is recovery + evening departure to Iguazu (no sightseeing). Feb 11–13: Iguazu Falls. All Rio distances are approximate from R. Santa Clara, 405, Copacabana.

Geographic Clusters from Airbnb

Cluster A — Corcovado / Santa Teresa / Lapa

Christ the Redeemer (Cosme Velho, ~7 km / 20 min) → Uber across to Santa Teresa (~15 min) → Selarón Steps → Lapa arches. Natural 6–7 hour sequence. Best: Feb 7 morning (first train 8am clear sky only). Backup if cloudy: reverse order, do Santa Teresa/Lapa first, reschedule Cristo.

Cluster B — Sugarloaf / Urca / Mirante Dona Marta

Sugarloaf cable car base at Praia Vermelha (~7 km / 15–20 min from Airbnb). After descent: Urca seafront walk (15 min). Optional: Mirante Dona Marta (~15 min Uber from Urca). Best: Feb 8 morning. Full loop: 3–4 hours.

Cluster C — Ipanema / Arpoador / Leblon

Ipanema Beach Posto 9 (~1.5 km / 5–10 min walk or Uber from Airbnb). Walk the sand west to Leblon (3.5 km, 30 min). Arpoador Rock on return (~1.4 km from Airbnb). Entirely walkable. Best: Feb 8 afternoon (Feb 11 is now Iguazu).

Cluster D — Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas

Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas (~4–5 km / 10–12 min Uber from Airbnb). The freshwater lagoon with mountain views and local kiosks (açaí, drinks). Not in the confirmed itinerary — Feb 10 is now recovery + evening departure to Iguazu. Best reserved for a future Rio visit.

Cluster E — Tijuca National Park

Vista Chinesa (~10 km / 25 min) + Mesa do Imperador + Cascatinha Taunay. Uber essential. Go before 10 AM to beat afternoon storms. Not on this itinerary (Feb 11 is now Iguazu) — see the dedicated Tijuca tab for a full plan. Best reserved for a future trip or a return trip.

Cluster F — Parque Lage (Tijuca edge)

Forest park at base of Corcovado (~6 km / 15–18 min from Airbnb). Free grounds, excellent café in the palace courtyard. Low-energy option — good for a light recovery day or when combining with Jardim Botânico or Cristo. 1–1.5 hours.

Carnival Night Transport — Feb 9

To Camarote Mar — Meeting Point First

Walk to meeting point: Othon Palace Copacabana (Av. Atlântica, 3264) is approximately 300m from R. Santa Clara, 405 — a 3–5 minute walk along the beach avenue. Camarote Mar organises transport from this meeting point to Sector 6 of the Sambadrome. Confirm departure time from your booking documentation. Do not attempt to go to the Sambadrome independently by Uber on a parade night — traffic gridlock is severe.

Return from Sambadrome — approx 4–5am

Return transfers are INCLUDED in your Camarote Mar ticket: after the final parade (~3 AM — Night 3 has 4 schools), buses run from the Sambadrome pickup area back to the Othon Palace meeting point, then the 5-min walk to the Airbnb. If returning independently: Metro Line 2 from Praça Onze (runs 24 hours on all three parade nights) → transfer at Central do Brasil → Line 1 → Siqueira Campos (Copa). Walk ~8 min to Airbnb. Do not try to take Uber directly from the Sambadrome exit at 5am — walk 2–3 blocks clear first before opening the app.

General Transport Notes

🚇

Metro 24-hour service: Runs all night on Feb 7, 8, and 9 only. Normal hours all other days. Line 1 serves Copacabana (Siqueira Campos, Cardeal Arcoverde). Line 2 connects to Sambadrome (Praça Onze). Transfer at Central do Brasil.

Uber during Carnival week

Expect 3–8× surge pricing throughout the week. From our Airbnb, always request pickup on interior streets (Rua Barata Ribeiro, Rua Ministro Viveiros de Castro) rather than Av. Atlântica, which closes during major bloco events. Install 99 alongside Uber — having both apps increases availability. Budget approximately R$30–80 per Uber trip within the South Zone depending on surge and destination.

Arpoador: ~1.4 km, 5–8 min walk · Ipanema Posto 9: ~1.5 km, 10 min walk · Siqueira Campos metro: ~800m, 8 min walk · Sugarloaf cable car base: ~7 km, 15–20 min Uber · Cristo Cosme Velho: ~7 km, 20–25 min Uber · Botanical Garden: ~6 km, 15–18 min Uber · Vista Chinesa: ~10 km, 25 min Uber · Sambadrome: ~8 km, 25 min (metro strongly preferred)
