Tijuca planning summary: In the confirmed itinerary, Feb 6–10 are the Rio days (Feb 10–14 is Iguazu). Tijuca does not fit within the Rio window — best suited to a return trip. If doing Tijuca: Uber into the park → Vista Chinesa (drive-up panorama) → Mesa do Imperador (same road, 2km) → Cascatinha Taunay (short waterfall walk) → return Uber. Covers the park's three most accessible highlights before afternoon storms arrive. Parque Lage is a separate, easier option closer to the Airbnb (15 min). Pico da Tijuca and Pedra da Gávea are full-day committed hikes best suited to a future trip.

Planning Window 2 · Extension Planning

Top 10 Tourist Destinations

Ten Brazilian destinations genuinely worth considering for a first — and possibly only — visit to Brazil. Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu Falls are already part of this trip and are excluded below. These 10 are numbered for readability, not ranked by absolute importance — each covers a fundamentally different side of Brazil.

1
Fernando de Noronha
Pernambuco · Atlantic Ocean · 350 km offshore
A UNESCO World Heritage archipelago and federal marine protected area — legally limited to ~500 visitors per day, which is the point. Brazil's finest beaches (Baía do Sancho, Praia do Leão) are consistently ranked among the best on earth. The marine ecosystem is extraordinary: spinner dolphins, sea turtles, reef sharks, and some of South America's best diving and snorkeling. Nothing in Brazil quite compares to this combination of pristine protected beaches, clear water, and wildlife.
Key experiences
  • Baía do Sancho — consistently rated one of the world's top beaches
  • Diving or snorkeling with spinner dolphins and sea turtles
  • Forte dos Remédios and volcanic geology
  • Mirante dos Golfinhos sunrise dolphin viewing
  • Boat tours around the archipelago
Ideal stay
4–6 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → Recife (REC) → Noronha (FEN) · ~4h total · book well ahead · limited seats
February
Good — sea turtle nesting peak season, dolphin activity high; rainy season brings brief afternoon showers but water remains warm and clear
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Pristine protected marine ecosystem, dramatically different beaches, marine wildlife — nothing in the main itinerary compares
2
Amazon Rainforest / Manaus
Amazonas · North Brazil
The world's largest tropical rainforest covers more than half of Brazil and is one of the most biodiverse ecosystems on earth. Manaus is the primary gateway — a city of 2 million people 1,500 km inland from the Atlantic, reachable only by plane or multi-day river boat. The "Meeting of the Waters" (where the dark Rio Negro meets the pale Amazon for kilometers without mixing) is one of Brazil's most iconic natural spectacles. The rainforest experience here is completely distinct from anything at Rio or Iguazu.
Key experiences
  • Meeting of the Waters (Encontro das Águas) — Negro meets Amazon
  • Jungle lodge stays with guided night walks and wildlife spotting
  • Piranha fishing and pink river dolphin encounters
  • Teatro Amazonas opera house — Belle Époque rubber-boom landmark
  • Flooded forest (igapó) canoe tours during high-water season
Ideal stay
4–5 days (2 in Manaus, 2–3 in jungle lodge)
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → MAO (Manaus) · ~4h direct · LATAM, Azul, GOL · daily flights
February
Good — high-water season (Feb–May); flooded forest accessible by canoe, pink dolphins more visible; heat and humidity are high year-round
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Amazon rainforest — the defining Brazilian ecosystem, entirely absent from the main itinerary
3
Pantanal
Mato Grosso do Sul / Mato Grosso · Central-West Brazil
The world's largest tropical wetland — roughly the size of France — is Brazil's best wildlife destination and one of the finest on earth for wildlife observation. Unlike the Amazon's dense canopy, the Pantanal's open wetlands make spotting jaguars, giant otters, tapirs, capybaras, caimans, and hundreds of bird species genuinely accessible. The Transpantaneira Road in the northern Pantanal is world-famous for wildlife density. UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
Key experiences
  • Jaguar spotting — Pantanal has the world's highest jaguar density
  • Giant otters, capybaras, tapirs, giant anteaters
  • Caimans and 650+ bird species (hyacinth macaws, jabiru storks)
  • Boat safaris on the Paraguay River
  • Fazenda (ranch) lodge stays on working cattle ranches
Ideal stay
3–5 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → Campo Grande (CGR) or Cuiabá (CGB) · ~2h · then lodge transfer (~2–3h road)
February
Acceptable — peak wet season; flooding limits road access and some areas. Dry season (Jul–Oct) is superior for wildlife. February is workable but requires lodge research on accessibility
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
World-class wildlife in an entirely different ecosystem — jaguar, giant otters, massive bird diversity; nothing like this anywhere in the main itinerary
4
Lençóis Maranhenses
Maranhão · Northeast Brazil · National Park
One of Brazil's most visually extraordinary landscapes: vast white sand dunes stretching 70 km along the coast, filled seasonally with thousands of fresh, clear turquoise and blue lagoons. This ecosystem exists nowhere else on earth — the combination of coastal dunes and rainfall-fed lagoons produces a surreal landscape that looks like a desert and a lake district simultaneously. A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve candidate with no comparable equivalent in the world.
Key experiences
  • Swimming in the crystal lagoons (Lagoa Azul, Lagoa Bonita)
  • Walking the white dune fields at sunrise or sunset
  • 4WD jeep tours through the park
  • Barreirinhas town as the main base
  • Lagoa da Gaivota panoramic viewpoint
Ideal stay
2–3 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → São Luís (SLZ) · ~3h · then 4WD transfer ~3–4h to Barreirinhas
February
Peak season — February is the best month; lagoons are at maximum fill from December rains. This is exactly when the landscape is most spectacular
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Unique landform found nowhere else on earth — white dune fields with swimming lagoons; no equivalent anywhere in the itinerary
5
Salvador
Bahia · Northeast Brazil · former Portuguese colonial capital
Brazil's first colonial capital and the historic center of Afro-Brazilian culture. The Pelourinho (UNESCO World Heritage Site) is one of Latin America's best-preserved colonial districts — baroque churches, colorful colonial buildings, and the living culture of candomblé (Afro-Brazilian religion), capoeira, and axé music. Salvador's Carnival, centered on trio elétrico trucks, is one of the largest street parties on earth and runs the same week as Rio Carnival — a genuinely different Carnival experience.
Key experiences
  • Pelourinho historic district — UNESCO baroque architecture
  • Carnival Salvador — February, world's largest street Carnival by attendance
  • Candomblé ceremonies and Afro-Brazilian cultural centers
  • Capoeira performances at the Mercado Modelo
  • Elevador Lacerda and Baía de Todos os Santos viewpoints
Ideal stay
3–4 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → SSA (Salvador) · ~2h direct · daily flights on Gol, LATAM, Azul
February
Peak event — Salvador Carnival runs the same week as Rio Carnival (Feb 7–11). Combining both is logistically complex; visiting before or after is recommended
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Afro-Brazilian cultural depth, UNESCO colonial history, entirely different Carnival tradition — nothing equivalent in the main itinerary
6
Chapada Diamantina
Bahia · Central Brazil · National Park
Brazil's premier hiking destination — a national park of mesas, canyons, waterfalls, caves, and crystal-clear natural pools in the interior of Bahia. Lençóis town is the base for multi-day treks to the Morro do Pai Inácio plateau, the underground blue lagoons of Gruta da Pratinha and Poço Azul, and the Cachoeira do Buracão waterfall canyon. Offers a fundamentally different experience from Brazil's coast — Atlantic rainforest remnants, endemic wildlife, and dramatic highland scenery.
Key experiences
  • Morro do Pai Inácio — mesa plateau with panoramic views
  • Poço Azul and Gruta da Pratinha — underground turquoise cave pools
  • Cachoeira do Buracão waterfall and canyon walk
  • Fumaça waterfall — one of Brazil's highest, visible from the rim
  • Multi-day trekking routes (Vale do Pati)
Ideal stay
4–5 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → SSA (Salvador) · ~2h · then 7h bus or 1h flight to Lençóis (LEC)
February
Good — rainy season brings waterfalls to maximum volume; trails can be muddy but spectacular; Poço Azul and Pratinha remain accessible; waterfalls at peak
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Highland national park, mountain hiking, underground cave pools, canyons — a completely interior Brazil experience absent from the coast/falls itinerary
7
Ouro Preto
Minas Gerais · Southeast Brazil · UNESCO World Heritage City
Brazil's finest surviving colonial baroque city — a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980 and one of the most architecturally intact 18th-century cities in the Americas. Built on gold-rush wealth in the 1700s, Ouro Preto's steep cobblestone hills are lined with baroque churches (13 UNESCO-protected), including the masterworks of sculptor Aleijadinho. The Museu da Inconfidência marks the site of Brazil's first independence movement. Entirely different from Rio's modernism and Iguazu's nature.
Key experiences
  • Igreja de São Francisco de Assis — Aleijadinho's baroque masterpiece
  • Praça Tiradentes and Museu da Inconfidência
  • Walking the colonial streetscape — cobblestones, baroque churches, fountains
  • Minas Gerais cuisine (pão de queijo, feijão tropeiro)
  • Day trips to Mariana and Congonhas (Aleijadinho prophets)
Ideal stay
2 days
Access from Rio
Bus from GIG or Novo Rio terminal · ~6.5h · or fly GIG → BHZ (Belo Horizonte) ~1h + 1.5h road transfer
February
Excellent — Ouro Preto runs one of Brazil's most atmospheric Carnivals (smaller than Rio, known for cultural events); summer is warm but manageable; fully accessible year-round
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Portuguese colonial baroque heritage — the only UNESCO colonial city on this itinerary; 18th-century architecture and Brazilian history unavailable in Rio or Iguazu
8
Jericoacoara
Ceará · Northeast Brazil · National Park
One of Brazil's most distinctive beach destinations — a small village with sand streets inside a national park, accessible only by 4WD across dunes or via unpaved road. The setting is unusually dramatic: sand dunes descending to the sea, freshwater lagoons (Lagoa do Paraíso, Lagoa Azul) 20 km inland, and the famous Pedra Furada rock arch. Conde Nast and Lonely Planet consistently list it among the world's most beautiful beaches. The village retains an authentic, relatively uncommercialized character rare for a destination of this calibre.
Key experiences
  • Sunset on the Duna do Pôr do Sol (daily ritual, every visitor)
  • Lagoa do Paraíso — translucent freshwater lagoon with hammocks
  • Pedra Furada rock arch on the beach
  • 4WD dune crossing to reach the village
  • Kitesurfing and windsurfing (peak Dec–Feb)
Ideal stay
3–4 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → Fortaleza (FOR) · ~3.5h · then 4WD transfer ~4h or bus + 4WD
Acceptable — Feb is the transition from peak wind season to low season; winds ease slightly. Beach and lagoons remain beautiful; less crowded than Jan. Rainy season starts March–April.
February
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Northeast beach with dunes and lagoons — an entirely different coastal landscape from Rio's urban beaches; the village remoteness and lagoon combination is unique
9
Bonito
Mato Grosso do Sul · Central-West Brazil
Brazil's leading eco-tourism destination, built around rivers of extraordinary clarity — filtered through limestone bedrock to a turquoise transparency that makes snorkeling among fish in natural rivers genuinely otherworldly. The Río Sucuri and Rio da Prata are the signature experiences. All activities require guided booking through the municipal tourism system (entry caps protect the ecosystem). Frequently listed alongside the Amazon and Pantanal as one of Brazil's three essential nature destinations.
Key experiences
  • Snorkeling Rio da Prata — crystal river with hundreds of dourado and pacu
  • Flutuação (river float) on the Río Sucuri
  • Abismo Anhumas — rappel into a cave lake with stalactites (advanced)
  • Gruta do Lago Azul — cave with brilliant blue underground lake
  • Lagoa Misteriosa — flooded cenote with 220m depth
Ideal stay
3–4 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → Campo Grande (CGR) · ~2h · then 5h bus or rental car (or Charter flight to Bonito airport)
February
Caveat — February is rainy season; heavy rain can cloud river visibility, reducing the snorkeling experience significantly. Dry season (Jun–Sep) is optimal. If visiting in Feb, check river conditions on arrival
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Crystal-clear limestone river snorkeling and cave systems — a completely different water experience from the falls at Iguazu; the transparency is unlike anything else in Brazil
10
Recife & Olinda
Pernambuco · Northeast Brazil · UNESCO World Heritage (Olinda)
Two complementary cities 6 km apart. Olinda is a UNESCO-listed colonial hilltop town with whitewashed baroque churches, a thriving arts scene, and one of Brazil's most beloved Carnivals — characterized by giant puppet figures (bonecos gigantes), frevo music, and street processions through colonial alleys. Recife (capital of Pernambuco) is the economic and cultural center of the Northeast, with the Recife Antigo historic district and a vibrant regional food culture centered on seafood and tapioca. Pernambuco is also the state containing Fernando de Noronha.
Key experiences
  • Olinda Carnival — giant puppet figures, frevo, street processions (February)
  • Olinda colonial architecture — 13 baroque churches on the UNESCO list
  • Recife Antigo — historic waterfront district and nightlife
  • Instituto Ricardo Brennand — world-class museum in a medieval castle
  • Northeast cuisine — moqueca pernambucana, tapioca, carne de sol
Ideal stay
2–3 days
Access from Rio
Fly GIG → REC (Recife/Guararapes) · ~3h direct · daily flights Gol, LATAM, Azul
February
Peak event — Olinda Carnival (same week as Rio Carnival) is one of Brazil's most celebrated. The two Carnivals coincide, so combining requires planning. Visit before or after the Rio trip
Adds vs. Rio + Iguazu
Northeast Carnival tradition, UNESCO baroque colonial culture, Afro-Brazilian Pernambuco roots — distinct from Rio's Sambadrome tradition and Bahia's axé music
Note on ranking: These 10 are numbered for readability, not presented as a strict scientific ranking. Each represents a fundamentally different Brazilian experience. The selection prioritises once-in-a-lifetime value, geographic diversity, and experience uniqueness — not proximity to Rio or general popularity. Sources: Visit Brasil, UNESCO World Heritage List, IBAMA, Lonely Planet Brazil, National Geographic Travel, Condé Nast Traveler, September 2026.

Neighborhood, safety, transport, and Carnival schedule sections are based on current research (September 2026).

Iguazu Falls · Feb 10–14, 2026

Iguazu Falls

4 days at one of the world's great natural wonders — 275 waterfalls spanning 2.7 km on the Brazil–Argentina border. Base: Foz do Iguaçu, Brazilian side. Arrive Feb 10, 6:40 PM (GOL G3 1866 · GIG Terminal 2 dep 4:25 PM), depart Feb 14 (7:55 PM).

Hotels Near the Falls

February is peak summer + Valentine's weekend. Sanma Hotel by Nobile is confirmed for Feb 10–14 — the Belmond (Hotel das Cataratas) remains the splurge alternative as the only hotel inside the national park, with after-hours falls access.

HotelDistance to FallsEst. Price / Night (Feb)

Border Crossing — Foz do Iguaçu → Puerto Iguazú

How to Cross

  • Cross via Tancredo Neves International Bridge (15 km from Foz city center)
  • Public bus from TTU terminal: ~R$15, 30 min + immigration stops
  • Guided hotel day-tour: most convenient — handles all transfers and logistics
  • Allow 1.5–2 hours total crossing time

Documents & Visas

  • Keep US passport accessible all day — needed at both immigration posts
  • Argentina: No visa required for US citizens
  • Brazil: eVisa required (applied before travel at brazil.vfsevisa.com · $80.90)
  • Exit stamp (Brazil) → Entry stamp (Argentina) → reverse on return

Currency

  • Brazil — Real (BRL): ~6 BRL per USD. ATMs widely available in Foz
  • Argentina — Peso (ARS): USD cash widely accepted and often preferred on the Argentine side
  • Paraguay — Guaraní (PYG): USD and BRL accepted in most Ciudad del Este stores

Getting Around Foz

  • Uber works well in the city and to the park
  • Bus Line 120: Foz city center → Brazilian park (~R$5, 40 min)
  • Taxi to park: R$50–80 one way (~20 min)
  • Hotels on Av. das Cataratas often have shuttle service

Pre-Travel Checklist

  • ☐ Brazil eVisa — apply at brazil.vfsevisa.com · $80.90 · allow 5 business days processing
  • ☐ Yellow Fever vaccine — at a travel clinic, at least 10 days before departure (required if visiting Paraguay)
  • ☐ Hepatitis A + Typhoid vaccines — CDC recommended for all Brazil travelers
  • ☑ Sanma Hotel by Nobile confirmed — Feb 10–14, near the Brazilian park entrance
  • ☐ Pre-purchase Argentine park entry — skip queues, especially for Devil's Throat train

Vegetarian Food Guide

Being fully vegetarian is straightforward in Foz. Brazil has a strong por kilo (pay-by-weight) buffet culture — vegetarian options are always abundant. Specify no meat clearly when ordering in Argentina.

Inside the Parks

  • Porto Canoas (Brazilian side) — terrace restaurant, vegetarian salads, pasta, river views. Good quality
  • La Selva (Argentine side) — pasta and salads; say "sin carne, sin pollo, sin pescado"
  • Kiosks on both trails — pão de queijo, fresh fruit, coconut water, granola bars

Foz do Iguaçu City

  • Cantina da Bea — all-you-can-eat heavily vegetarian buffet. Best dinner option
  • Cheiro Verde — dedicated vegetarian/vegan buffet (por kilo)
  • Pop Art Café — vegan and vegetarian café, gluten-free options. Great for breakfast
  • La Strega — Italian, full vegan menu: pumpkin ravioli, vegetable pasta
  • Vô Luiz Pizzeria — excellent vegetarian pizzas and pasta

Puerto Iguazú, Argentina

  • The Argentine Experience — vegetarian empanadas, interactive dinner. Book in advance
  • Terra Wok & Grill — varied menu, vegetarian-friendly

Ordering tip: "Soy vegetariano/a — sin carne, sin pollo, sin pescado" (no meat, no chicken, no fish).

Brazilian Staples — Naturally Vegetarian

  • Pão de queijo — warm cheese bread, found everywhere
  • Açaí bowls — thick açaí with granola, banana, honey
  • Tapioca crepes — cheese or coconut-filled
  • Fresh sucos — maracujá, mango, guava, caju juices
  • Vitaminas — thick blended tropical fruit shakes

Health & Disease Risk

Consult a travel health clinic at least 4–6 weeks before departure to get vaccinated in time.

Yellow Fever

Vaccine Recommended

Get at a travel clinic ≥10 days before travel. Proof required for Paraguay entry after being in Brazil.

Malaria

No Risk

CDC confirms zero malaria risk in Foz do Iguaçu. No medication needed.

Dengue

Present — Feb Peak

Use DEET repellent 30%+ all day. Aedes mosquitoes bite during daylight hours, not just at night.

Hepatitis A

Vaccine Recommended

CDC recommends for all travelers to Brazil regardless of itinerary.

Typhoid

Vaccine Recommended

Especially relevant when eating local or street food. Shot or 2-week oral course.

Zika

Low Risk

Present at low levels. Consult doctor if pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

What to Pack

☐ Poncho (buy in park ~$5 or bring your own)

☐ Quick-dry shorts and t-shirts

☐ Waterproof sandals (Chacos, Tevas)

☐ Waterproof dry bag for phone and camera

☐ DEET repellent 30%+ (Sawyer / Off! Deep Woods)

☐ Sunscreen SPF 50 + wide-brim hat + sunglasses

☐ Spare set of clothes in a sealed dry bag

☐ Oral rehydration salts for heat/humidity days
